sent_emails.body: Thanks Jon, Yes – there is an individual identifier for each point, and the results will be aligned to those points. We are required to take 4 sample points within each of the 4-strata areas that make up a project boundary. We have stratified (4x strata) based on soil type, slope, and a range of other factors based on our HORIZON model. Reserve points, are additional points within each strata that we will take, if a primary target point cannot be obtained. We did have to use some reserve points on the property to complete the sampling. From: Will Frecheville > Sent: Thursday, 9 April 2026 10:36 AM To: Justin Costello > Cc: Claudia Bryant >; Dylan Jones > Subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. sent_emails.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - McClean CP
sent_emails.body: Dear Justin, Congratulations on having the McClean CP issued ACCUs following our submission of the Offsets Report. Please see attached Certificate of Entitlement for the issuance. The project has been issued 4942 ACCUs. I have also attached the Statement of Account for you, which outlines the amount of ACCUs that you are now entitled to. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. sent_emails.subject: Re-Introduction to AgriProve: Soil Carbon Projects and Offer for Farm Visit
sent_emails.body: Dear Sam Thanks for the chat- I appreciated your time and the chance to talk through what soil carbon could mean for your operation. I know you have looked at soil projects before, and am pleased to be able to present again to you how AgriProve can work with you to support your farming operation. Our aim is to make Soil Carbon accessible and beneficial for farmers. Our job is to take the complexity off your plate, maximize your credits, and make sure you're partnered with a developer you can trust for the long term. We've backed that up with results - 600+ registered projects, 75%+ market share of Australian soil carbon projects, and 123,000+ ACCUs issued to primary producers. We were the first to deliver soil carbon credits to Australian farmers and remain the fastest crediting developer in the market. There have been some updates since you last looked at soil carbon projects: * → A tailored project designed around your farming system * → Annual crediting potential through our HORIZON platform - no more waiting five years * → Full transparency on your ACCU account and credit delivery * → A dedicated specialist guiding you from eligibility through to income Key resources (click links provided below) * → AgriProve Information Pack * → Project Case Studies * → Portfolio Map - see projects near you * → Eligible Practices & Building Carbon Guide * → Create your free AgriProve platform account As mentioned, we have a grazier in residence on the road with AgriProve at the moment that I'd love to arrange to come out your way for a short visit - an hour at most, entirely on your terms. sent_emails.body: Hi Ella, Picking this up for Claudia. Some points for clarification. You then have ownership of those ACCUs and are not obliged to sell for a fixed or spot price. Additionally, if you do choose to sell, there is no obligation to sell through AgriProve. sent_emails.body: Hi Alison, Thank you for your email and picking this up. We agree with your assessment. And accept this change. Please see attached 260105 – Sandalwood CP – T1 Offsets Report_v3 (2). The sequestration for the period is 758.2 tC; Net Abatement 2763 tCOwe; revised ACCU claim of 2072 ACCUs. Explainer: In the submitted 260105 – Sandalwood CP – T1 Offsets Report_v3, Column BP of the SOC Supplement Tab, the cell was pulling data incorrectly from the lab results for that sample. The correct cell that equation S6 (Column BP) should have been pulling from was the corresponding row in column BA; which is the gravimetric organic carbon content of the oven dry whole soil. (Equation S12). This has been corrected for the T0 round where this was identified. The other equations were inspected and identified as correct. sent_emails.subject: RE: Re: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Next Steps
sent_emails.body: Hi Mark and Amanda, Following on from our visit and checking in with the severe weather that is occurring in your region. Have you had any further questions regarding project design, mapping or registration intent following on from our conversation a fortnight ago? From my notes, the topics we discussed were: Core Concern: Project Design & Configuration Your primary concern was whether work done in certain areas (specifically high country) would materially increase the baseline or disadvantage them. We have addressed this by configuring the project by isolating the high country into a specific project, demonstrating the design was built with their best interests in mind while maximising usability. We will work with you to register projects as you want – we can align this to implementation, baselining or ability for success. It may be that we register the two highest potential projects in the near term, and then look to work out how best to maximise the leucaena country that is more advanced in the carbon and farm improvement approach. Key Context You want to set this project up in line with family succession planning, with your overriding priority is setting it up for long-term success and maximising carbon credit (ACCU) potential. Project Proponent Discussion Your lawyers had advised you to act as project proponent to maintain control of ACCUs. We will set up an ANREU account that your entitlement of ACCUs produced will be transferred to you within 10-business days of being issued, you will have full control for your share of ACCUs. As we discussed, I clarified the additional regulatory and compliance responsibilities that come with that role, and why having those obligations managed externally gives the project the best chance of compliance and success. Implementation / Grazing Management You intend to make grazing management changes but are not interested in intensive cell grazing — you want a more holistic, flexible approach. you want someone on-site to assess what changes are realistic and where the opportunities lie. We can provide you with a video call with our Grazier in Residence (Hobbs Magaret); he will happily provide you with some tangible practice changes that can align to your overall philosophy. We will not likely be able to have Hobbs come to farm, as he is based in Albury. Baseline & Costs Baseline sampling costs were discussed. The upfront cost is not insignificant, but the framing was that carbon income is supplementary — cream on top of the farming enterprise. As mentioned, the baseline costs will be as quoted in the KCT that you have received and is inclusive of all projects, we invoice this on a project by project basis, so there may be a phased costing approach for the baseline sampling, depending on when this occurs. We are also flexible if you choose to split some between upfront payment and future ACCUs (if in the event no ACCUs are generated, this amount is payable at 5-years as per the $ amount (not the ACCU number multiplied by spot price); or on project termination prior to projects being awarded ACCUs.). @Mark – please send through the list of questions that you had, that you raised in the meeting. I will endeavour to respond to these questions as quickly as possible. sent_emails.subject: RE: Feedback from solicitors
sent_emails.body: Hi Dan and Emma-Jane, Thank-you again for taking the time to meet with me on Tuesday. I greatly appreciated the visit and the opportunity to discuss in further detail the Stonehaven Soil Carbon Project. Following up on our conversations and the actions that I have committed to you from that meeting, please see below: Action Item: Clarifications to clauses 13.3 and 14.3 to align with the explanations in the letter. This is a two part approach, firstly, we are happy to include these explanations as an appendix to the Key Commercial Terms, that we can sign-off and agree on. Clarification of Project Termination (once again, happy to include this into the appendix, so that it is agreed and signed). 13. Default and Termination 13.1 Where there is an Event of Default which is not remedied within 30 Business Days the non-defaulting party may choose to terminate this Agreement by giving written notice to the defaulting party. Event of Default means: (1) a material breach of this Agreement; (2) any failure to pay any amount or transfer any ACCUs in accordance with the Agreement; or (3) an Insolvency Event. 13.3 states: “Operator may terminate this Agreement if the parties, acting in good faith, agree there is no reasonable pathway to keep the Carbon Projects operational. In such circumstances, the Operator must: …” Under the Default and Termination clause, and assuming the agreement has not been terminated in line with Clause 2.3 (i.e. the project in unviable prior to the first reporting and issuance of ACCUs), AgriProve does not have rights to terminate the agreement. Clause 13.3 requires that both parties agree to terminate the project while acting in good faith. If AgriProve were to instigate and insist on a project termination due to our assessment that it was unviable for AgriProve to continue, you as a landholder/operator have the rights within this agreement to deny that termination of the project. If AgriProve were to continue down this path without your consent, then it would be likely be determined that we would be in breach of our good faith obligations, and that would constitute a material breach of the agreement. We would then be required to pay all costs associated and outlined as per 13.2. If the project was revoked, it would be our responsibility to return all ACCUs to the project, as we would have materially breached the agreement. This is of course, under the assumption that you as a landholder have: * Complied with all obligations under the LMS and Methodology * Reasonably believe the project remains viable for your business * Declines to agree that the termination is necessary. The second part, are the following drafted clauses: Amendment to 13.3(2) - (2) pay all outstanding fees and costs owed to AgriProve including the equivalent dollar value of any Additional Product and Services Fee ACCUs previously agreed. For the avoidance of doubt, where no Project ACCUs have been issued to the Carbon Projects as at the date of termination under this clause 13.3, and any baseline soil sampling costs have been met by the Operator in accordance with clause 8.2, no further fees or costs shall be payable by the Operator or Landholder to AgriProve; Lastly, and as discussed, it is not in our interest to revoke projects, this is out of line with our business strategy. If there was no pathway for our relationship to continue, and operate the project, then it would be transferring the project proponent and removal of AgriProve from project operation as per Clause 9. Please let me know any feedback following the above, and we can progress. I think (outside of the previously updated clauses (Biosecurity)) and the amendment to 13.3(2), the simplest option rather than re-drafting clauses, is to add the explanations and statements made in these emails as an appendix, and if approved, we can incorporate as an appendix to the KCT; so it is clear and agreed. Thanks again for your time on Tuesday, Kind regards, Will Frecheville | Head of Operat…

As they stand, no commercial agreement was put in place between Paraway and AgriProve, so we’d want to come to some formal arrangement moving forward. I believe there had been some past discussions around the 25% AgriProve success fee on future ACCUs, and Paraway seeking to retain 100% of ACCU issuances. Both the Perry’s Paddock and Steam Plains Carbon Projects exhibit positive trends in their satellite-derived NDRE data indicators since the projects were baselined in 2020. This suggests it would be worthwhile resampling the projects to obtain another round of soil data to compare their respective carbon stocks. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project’s registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? Can you specify which date the implementation activities started. * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. Last communications from you regarding the above email was that you were needing to determine whether you wished this project to continue. If this is the case, the above items will need to be actions with urgency. We will need to complete the subsequent resampling prior to 15-November-2025. We will need to as a first step have the AgriProve commercial agreement signed, and we can have some discussions on the broader ACCU commercial arrangement. sent_emails.subject: Re: Thorby CP project start date variation
sent_emails.body: P {margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0;} Hi Dylan, Yes, on all fronts, with one minor tweak - the implementation is referenced to the start date, so as long as it's after the (new) date of 11/02/2023 it's fine. It's unlikely that there would be a significant increase in SOC between then and the baseline date. This is also only relevant if the eligible activity as originally proposed is the same (i.e. Use of the same fertiliser). If the new landholders are looking at addressing the nutrients in a different way to the original eligible activity, that is still different to the baseline, we can update the LMS/CPP, and vary the start date. Logic is sound, and I think that is a good approach. If implementation has occurred, then we can vary the start date to the day before the project activity was implemented, however, the new landholders will lose any carbon built between the non-compliant baseline and the compliant baseline. From memory though, there was a reasonable decrease in SOC Stocks between T0 and T1 from those projects, so the landholders may not have lost any potential. Let me know if you need anything else. The first two to show validated measured increases have generated a combined total of 9,214 ACCUs under the ACCU Scheme in a partnership with AgriProve, Australia’s leading carbon soiltech developer. Utilising AgriProve’s innovative, digitally enabled Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) model the projects benefited from the expedited soil sampling and carbon crediting process. The result is AgriProve partnering landholders can be issued ACCUs in two years instead of five. sent_emails.subject: Soil Carbon Testing
sent_emails.body: Hi Katrina, It was great to chat yesterday, and so good to hear students taking an interest in carbon farming, sustainable Ag and soil science. As promised, please see attached "Supplement to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology" that the Australian Methodology and ACCU scheme use to measure and quantify %SOC in soil. So you don't have to read the entire thing, I've summarised the key processes that the laboratories use to test for SOC. The releant sections are Part D, 2.0 Sample Preparation (page 20-21) 3.1 - Measuring gravimetric soil organic carbon content (p21 - 26) The method requires dry combustion analysis either by: * ASPAC Code 6B2b (Total Organic Carbon by Dumas, high-temperature combustion with no pre-treatment) for soils not containing carbonates * ASPAC Code 6B3 (total organic carbon by Duman high temperature combustion carbon with prior chemical removal of carbonates) for soils that do contain carbonates The other option, is the use of the Walkely-Black method. But this is not used in the Australian Method, but is commonly accepted as a high-integrity test. I hope this helps you and your student, please let me know if you'd be interested in being notified of our webinars, and upcoming events particularly relating to the soil-science. Alternatively, you can look at our youtube channel( https://www.youtube.com/@agriprove1642) which has a number of webinars on soil biology that you may find useful. Thanks again for chatting, hope to keep the conversation going soon. sent_emails.body: Hi John, To further clarify the below: Methodology Reference Amount Change Comment Change in soil organic carbon stock in the CEA with a specified probability of exceedance for a reporting period (Eqn69) 975.2 tC Inclusive of the first reporting period discount of 25% on estimated stocks. Change in soil organic carbon stock in the project are for the reporting period (Eq6) (Refer to below) 563.2 tC / 2065.8 tCO2e - 412 tC / 1,510.667 tCO2e -412 tC is the Q_NSF,CEA, as the total tonnes of Carbon added to the CEA in the form of non-synthetic fertiliser during the reporting period. In this case, it is the amount of carbon in the drinking water sludge, as specified in the farm records) Emissions due to performing the eligible activities on the project area 82.84 tCO2e (Net increase of 41.42 tCO2e vs baseline per year) Inclusive of the livestock increases, and emissions due to the AgriAsh and Drinking Water Sludge being considered ‘Lime’ Estimated Net Abatement 1982.96 (2065.8 tCO2e – 82.84 tCO2e); -82.84 TCO2e Change in SOC_RP.PA (Eqn 6) – Emissions_RP.PA – converted into tCO2e ACCU Estimation 1487 -25% -495.96 tCO2e Net Abatement(NAN), less CER Risk of Reversal Discount (5%) and Permanence Period Discount (20%). Calculated as NAN – (NAN*RoR[5%])-(NAN*Perm.Period[20%]) Rounded down to the nearest whole number. Landholder Entitlement 1116 -25%, -371 tCO2e Estimated ACCUs after AgriProve is paid our 25% success fee. With any partial ACCU being distributed to the landholder, to ensure AgriProve’s success fee is never more than 25%. Equation 6 [cid:image010.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] Where: [cid:image011.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] [cid:image012.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] This means that in order to determine the amount of change in carbon stock in the project area for the reporting period, we need to deduct any non-synthetic fertiliser that contains carbon from the change in carbon measured and reported to you prior to gathering farm records. In this instance, the organic carbon content (as supplied, and by using the Walkley-Black Method, it is safe to assume that is organic carbon) is 12.5% per L applied, and the quantity applied is equivalent to 168 tC and 244 tC is as detailed in the farm records. We must, as specified by the method, deduct this addition from the measured change in soil carbon stocks. It is also worth noting, that if we did not, that both the auditors and CER would identify this, and we would be required to deduct this amount at their insistence. It is important to note a couple of things here: 1. This is the first offsets report, at year 2 in a 25-year project. It has the 25% first reporting discount applied to the carbon stock, prior to any other discounts – this will be removed in the next reporting period. 2. If, the carbon levels are maintained, and the drinking sludge is not applied during a reporting period, and a claim is made for ACCUs, then the tonnes of carbon in the sludge will not be deducted from the change in carbon stock as it has been for this round. 3. For a 48Ha project, an increase and project ACCU claim (estimated) of 1487 ACCUs, is an astoundingly good result, and is the equivalent of 15.5 ACCUs/Ha/Yr. As an estimation of ‘sequestration’ this is 4.22 tC/Ha/yr. 4. This result may change depending on the auditors/CER determination, and is not final. Please call me if you wish to discuss. engagements.body: You don't often get email from john@soilregen.com.au. Learn why this is important Hi Michael, Thanks for the report and background info. This is to confirm that I'm happy for you to come and resample our project within the period of 29th Jan ~ 1 June. Regards, John John Lawson MEngSc (UNSW) Dip Tech Civ Eng (NSWIT/UTS) Director SoilRegen Pty Ltd 376 Blakney Creek Road North, BLAKNEY CREEK NSW 2581 Mobile: 0438 873 475 Ph: +61 438 873 475, ABN: 38 168 154 327 [cid:image007.jpg@01DA4E3B.7174ADC0] We recycle industrial byproducts to improve soil structure and biology for better crops and stock From: AgriProve Sent: Tuesday, January 23, 2024 12:16 PM To: John Lawson Subject: Request to resample Killen Carbon Project Hi John, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of 29th Jan ~ 1 June? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. Also, regarding your email yesterday. If there is a measured increase (likely based on previous discussions) we can resample in a 6 ~12 months after the sampled round. If next week is a goer please let me know asap. engagements.subject: RE: Killen CP - Farm Records
engagements.body: Hi John, To further clarify the below: Methodology Reference Amount Change Comment Change in soil organic carbon stock in the CEA with a specified probability of exceedance for a reporting period (Eqn69) 975.2 tC Inclusive of the first reporting period discount of 25% on estimated stocks. Change in soil organic carbon stock in the project are for the reporting period (Eq6) (Refer to below) 563.2 tC / 2065.8 tCO2e - 412 tC / 1,510.667 tCO2e -412 tC is the Q_NSF,CEA, as the total tonnes of Carbon added to the CEA in the form of non-synthetic fertiliser during the reporting period. In this case, it is the amount of carbon in the drinking water sludge, as specified in the farm records) Emissions due to performing the eligible activities on the project area 82.84 tCO2e (Net increase of 41.42 tCO2e vs baseline per year) Inclusive of the livestock increases, and emissions due to the AgriAsh and Drinking Water Sludge being considered ‘Lime’ Estimated Net Abatement 1982.96 (2065.8 tCO2e – 82.84 tCO2e); -82.84 TCO2e Change in SOC_RP.PA (Eqn 6) – Emissions_RP.PA – converted into tCO2e ACCU Estimation 1487 -25% -495.96 tCO2e Net Abatement(NAN), less CER Risk of Reversal Discount (5%) and Permanence Period Discount (20%). Calculated as NAN – (NAN*RoR[5%])-(NAN*Perm.Period[20%]) Rounded down to the nearest whole number. Landholder Entitlement 1116 -25%, -371 tCO2e Estimated ACCUs after AgriProve is paid our 25% success fee. With any partial ACCU being distributed to the landholder, to ensure AgriProve’s success fee is never more than 25%. Equation 6 [cid:image010.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] Where: [cid:image011.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] [cid:image012.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] This means that in order to determine the amount of change in carbon stock in the project area for the reporting period, we need to deduct any non-synthetic fertiliser that contains carbon from the change in carbon measured and reported to you prior to gathering farm records. In this instance, the organic carbon content (as supplied, and by using the Walkley-Black Method, it is safe to assume that is organic carbon) is 12.5% per L applied, and the quantity applied is equivalent to 168 tC and 244 tC is as detailed in the farm records. We must, as specified by the method, deduct this addition from the measured change in soil carbon stocks. It is also worth noting, that if we did not, that both the auditors and CER would identify this, and we would be required to deduct this amount at their insistence. It is important to note a couple of things here: 1. This is the first offsets report, at year 2 in a 25-year project. It has the 25% first reporting discount applied to the carbon stock, prior to any other discounts – this will be removed in the next reporting period. 2. If, the carbon levels are maintained, and the drinking sludge is not applied during a reporting period, and a claim is made for ACCUs, then the tonnes of carbon in the sludge will not be deducted from the change in carbon stock as it has been for this round. 3. For a 48Ha project, an increase and project ACCU claim (estimated) of 1487 ACCUs, is an astoundingly good result, and is the equivalent of 15.5 ACCUs/Ha/Yr. As an estimation of ‘sequestration’ this is 4.22 tC/Ha/yr. 4. This result may change depending on the auditors/CER determination, and is not final. Please call me if you wish to discuss. engagements.subject: Killen CP - Site Audit Visit - Tuesday 18th June
engagements.body: Hi John, In preparation for the Site Visit on Tuesday 18th June, I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. Please see the attached agenda for the site visit, and a couple of aspects that will be discussed as well as the following questions. 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of FMR dates) 2. Detailed description of all land management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points. Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically farm house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the farm, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to farm house/office - interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that farm records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the farm records (such as livestock, invoices for inputs (AgriAsh, DWT Sludge), contracts or invoices or records of spreading/incorporations of activities * Confirmation that we (yourself and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the Carbon project operation, implementation and administration I am happy to set up a meeting with you later next week to discuss this in further detail. Please let me know if you have any availability. engagements.body: Hi Will, Can you please clarify from the table below, that if we hold the carbon we added (421tC) at the T2 measurement, we’ll get the 1,510.667 tCO2e back? That is, the 421 tonnes doesn’t get added to the T0 baseline. Regards, John John Lawson MEngSc (UNSW) Dip Tech Civ Eng (NSWIT/UTS) Director SoilRegen Pty Ltd 376 Blakney Creek Road North, BLAKNEY CREEK NSW 2581 Mobile: 0438 873 475 Ph: +61 438 873 475, ABN: 38 168 154 327 Web: www.soilregen.com.au [cid:image001.jpg@01DB163B.91F9F280] We recycle industrial byproducts to improve soil structure and biology for better crops and stock From: Will Frecheville Sent: Thursday, 23 May 2024 10:07 AM To: John Lawson Subject: RE: Killen CP - Farm Records Hi John, To further clarify the below: Methodology Reference Amount Change Comment Change in soil organic carbon stock in the CEA with a specified probability of exceedance for a reporting period (Eqn69) 975.2 tC Inclusive of the first reporting period discount of 25% on estimated stocks. Change in soil organic carbon stock in the project are for the reporting period (Eq6) (Refer to below) 563.2 tC / 2065.8 tCO2e - 412 tC / 1,510.667 tCO2e -412 tC is the Q_NSF,CEA, as the total tonnes of Carbon added to the CEA in the form of non-synthetic fertiliser during the reporting period. In this case, it is the amount of carbon in the drinking water sludge, as specified in the farm records) Emissions due to performing the eligible activities on the project area 82.84 tCO2e (Net increase of 41.42 tCO2e vs baseline per year) Inclusive of the livestock increases, and emissions due to the AgriAsh and Drinking Water Sludge being considered ‘Lime’ Estimated Net Abatement 1982.96 (2065.8 tCO2e – 82.84 tCO2e); -82.84 TCO2e Change in SOC_RP.PA (Eqn 6) – Emissions_RP.PA – converted into tCO2e ACCU Estimation 1487 -25% -495.96 tCO2e Net Abatement(NAN), less CER Risk of Reversal Discount (5%) and Permanence Period Discount (20%). Calculated as NAN – (NAN*RoR[5%])-(NAN*Perm.Period[20%]) Rounded down to the nearest whole number. Landholder Entitlement 1116 -25%, -371 tCO2e Estimated ACCUs after AgriProve is paid our 25% success fee. With any partial ACCU being distributed to the landholder, to ensure AgriProve’s success fee is never more than 25%. Equation 6 [cid:image002.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] Where: [cid:image003.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] [cid:image004.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] This means that in order to determine the amount of change in carbon stock in the project area for the reporting period, we need to deduct any non-synthetic fertiliser that contains carbon from the change in carbon measured and reported to you prior to gathering farm records. In this instance, the organic carbon content (as supplied, and by using the Walkley-Black Method, it is safe to assume that is organic carbon) is 12.5% per L applied, and the quantity applied is equivalent to 168 tC and 244 tC is as detailed in the farm records. We must, as specified by the method, deduct this addition from the measured change in soil carbon stocks. It is also worth noting, that if we did not, that both the auditors and CER would identify this, and we would be required to deduct this amount at their insistence. It is important to note a couple of things here: 1. This is the first offsets report, at year 2 in a 25-year project. It has the 25% first reporting discount applied to the carbon stock, prior to any other discounts – this will be removed in the next reporting period. 2. If, the carbon levels are maintained, and the drinking sludge is not applied during a reporting period, and a claim is made for ACCUs, then the tonnes of carbon in the sludge will not be deducted from the change in carbon stock as it has been for this round. 3. For a 48Ha project, an increase and project ACCU claim (estimated) of 1487 ACCUs, is an astoundingly good result, and is the equivalent of 15.5 ACCUs/Ha/Yr. As an estimation of ‘sequestration’ this is 4.22 tC/Ha/yr. 4. This result may change depending on the auditors/CE…

engagements.body: Hi John, Assuming that you maintain the carbon level in the soil (and the tests confirm as such), and you do not add any additional carbon, you will get the 421tC back at the next reporting period. As the way the calculations worked, was that it was a deduction due to accounting for the addition of carbon to the land. Assuming that you do not add in any more carbon, then this proportion of the equation will go to zero, and therefore the amount will be as measured. engagements.subject: Trophy CP (CRD207716) [SEC=OFFICIAL]
engagements.body: OFFICIAL Regarding the Trophy CP (CRD207716), we have identified a few matters in the crediting application. 1. The LMS states that the project proposes to undertake three activities: application of nutrients, re‑establishment of pasture, and alteration of the stocking rate. It is unclear what activities have been undertaken during the reporting period. The Executive Summary indicates that only re‑establishment of pasture and alteration of the stocking rate were completed, however the summary in the Offsets Report states that all three proposed activities have been undertaken. Could you please confirm which version is correct, noting that there is minimal information in the Executive Summary regarding the application of nutrients in the project area? If only two of the three activities have been implemented to date, could you clarify whether the landholder intends to implement all three activities over the project period, or only the two described in the Executive Summary? Please provide this information by the 10th of February 2026. 1. The calculation of project emissions has a few errors: * Livestock emissions: The Offsets Report states that historical stocking rate data was available for the entire baseline period. However, there are entries in equation 16 which suggests that historical records were not available for maiden ewes (eq. 16 also includes entries for other ewes for which historical records were available, perhaps these entries are supposed to be for breeding ewes?). Emissions from maiden ewes (output of equation 15) were not included in the livestock emission calculations (equation 12), and it is unclear whether maiden ewes (and breeding ewes) were present during the baseline period. It is noted that maiden and breeding ewes were present during the reporting period. * Synthetic fertiliser emissions: The incorrect emissions factor in equation 19 was applied for both the baseline and reporting periods. The Queensland value for cotton was used (2.59) instead of the Victoria value for non‑irrigated pasture (1.72). * Baseline and reporting periods: Livestock emissions appear to have been reported over six years rather than five years over both periods; in particular, 365 days were applied to each year during the baseline period. We note that the issue of incorrect baseline periods has previously been raised in regards to other Agriprove projects. As correction of the above errors still result in a negative change in project emissions, an amended offset report is not required to be submitted for this crediting application. However, please address the above matters in the next crediting application. It would also speed up the assessment process for all Agriprove projects if it could be ensured that Offsets Reports for all projects are accurate and consistent with the method. engagements.body: Dear Jeremy, Please see the updated LMS 'Universal Land Management Strategy' which applies to the 2021 soil carbon method. I have also provided an NDRE report that reflects the entirety of the reporting period as requested. The previous NDRE report provided did not extend to the reporting period end date as it was part of our annual review process for the project. This process utilizes NDRE data for the 5-year baseline period of the project compared against the post-baseline or implementation period of the project. Positive change in the 5th percentile and mean NDRE data in the implementation period relative to the baseline provides an assessment of how the project is performing and allows a decision to be made whether the project will proceed to resampling. engagements.subject: Request for information - Lloyd Carbon Projects 1-8 [SEC=OFFICIAL]
engagements.body: Hi Cassandra, Apologies for my late response. Please see my responses to the requests for further information below for Lloyd Carbon Projects 1-8. Selected activity: Applying nutrients to the land in the form of a synthetic or non-synthetic fertilizer to address a material deficiency. Information required: Please specify what nutrient/s the soil in the project area is deficient in, and how the nutrient deficiency will be targeted in the form of a synthetic or non-synthetic fertilizer. * Plant tissue tests show general micronutrient deficiency in crops and pastures. The landholder will be using a new process of bio fermentation to produce foliar fertilisers, which will be a general mix containing most minerals to increase plant levels. The bio fermentation process makes nutrients more bioavailable to plants and is an efficient way of applying them. The landholder plans to make more specific blends in the future as experience is increased. This activity of making and applying bio ferments to address general nutrient deficiencies is therefore materially different from the baseline period and satisfies the relevant legislative requirements for management activities that are materially different from the baseline. Selected activity: Retaining stubble after a crop is harvested. Information required: Describe how the change from combine form tines to discs will retain stubble better, after a harvest. * The change from combine form tynes to discs for seeding allows for stubble to be retained after harvest, as a major benefit of disc seeding is the ability to plant through high standing residue/stubble loads. Tynes do not allow enough clearance to plant into heavy stubbles and can create clumping and machinery blockages that obstructs the seed row area and reduces emergence due to the inability to handle residue/stubble. Therefore, using combine form tynes requires the removal through slashing/baling/burning of stubble to allow for successful planting and crop establishment. Disc seeders can handle high standing stubble loads without clumping as they have improved residue handling capacity and inter-row sowing capabilities. This means that a practice change to using a disc seeder for planting will allow for stubble to be retained after harvest in a cropping and mixed system. Selected activity: Using a cover crop to promote soil vegetation cover or improve soil health, or both. Information required: The baseline management history table shows from 2021 there was cover crop sown (vetch, barely, wheat, peas, radish, turnips, millet, sorghum, sunflowers, buckwheat & canola). How will this activity be materially different from the baseline? * A feasibility assessment of a summer and winter mixed species cover crop consisting of vetch, barely, wheat, peas, radish, turnips, millet, sorghum, sunflowers, buckwheat & canola was conducted on limited areas of the property to assess the impacts on health and productivity of the winter crops which were harvested. The first feasibility assessment was in 2021 and was limited to 8 hectares, and further expanded in 2022 and 2023 based on positives results in plant health. The intention of the landholder is to implement a comprehensive summer and winter cover cropping system across the entire property as the projects progress. Please see the maps below which show where the feasibility assessments were located. engagements.body: OFFICIAL Hi Will, Thanks for the RFI information. Regarding the mapping of exclusion areas and emissions accounting areas, satellite imagery suggests that part of the land included in exclusion areas may be used for agricultural activities (see image below). As per Schedule 1 s5(5)(a) of the method, exclusion areas cannot include land where land management or agricultural activities are carried out. Instead, these areas should be defined as emissions accounting areas. Additionally, emissions accounting areas must distinctly separate to CEAs and exclusion areas, as per Schedule 1 s5(6). engagements.body: OFFICIAL Hi Imogen, The following was sent to the project primary contact via Online Services: Further information is required by the Clean Energy Regulator (the Regulator) to assess whether your application made under s31 of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Act 2011 (the CFI Act) meets the eligibility requirements for the variation of the declaration of an eligible offsets project. This notice to give information has been made by the Regulator in accordance with s26(1) of the Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative) Rule 2015 (the CFI Rule). S26(1) of the CFI Rule enables the Regulator to require, by written notice, an applicant to give the Regulator, within the period specified in the notice, further information in connection with the application. Formalising our approval process - customer facing materials
engagements.body: All, With our growth strategy gathering momentum - the amount of materials that go “customer facing” is on the up. It will be no news to any of you the risks that are inherent in this from both reputational and compliance perspectives. So, it’s time to formalise an approach. It’s very simple, but will add time and you will need to plan time for an approval process. What’s the Approval process? 1. Any customer facing material (for now), but we’ll likely need to extend this later. 2. Must have a review and approval from AB, KW and DW before going to SU. 3. The author requesting an approval from SU must include either the email chain or attach the emails with the approvals. 4. AB, KW and DW – in your review you are accountable for, grammar, formatting, brand, tone of voice, technical and process accuracy. By the time it gets to SU it should be in tip top shape. You may think this is a pain. But reflect on every typo you’ve picked up in an email you’ve received. How you’ve commented on poor formatting, confusing messaging or thought. “I got the same detail from someone else yesterday”, or worse still “someone told me something different yesterday”. The idea is to make sure that everything we do is high quality and consistent. Thanks TH Toby Hedgeland | Head of Product and Delivery [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: 0466602196 Email: toby@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [AgriProve Email Signature Designs (3).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image004.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image005.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] [cid:image006.png@01DA6FE8.F7AFCB80] Here at we care for your privacy. Explanation for the delayed reporting of the first reporting period, and relevant correspondence with the CER Projects were in Operation with Corporate Carbon acting as project proponent. Corporate Carbon's responsibility in a JV with Regenerative Australian Farmers (RAF) was to secure a Carbon Aabtement Contract, and assist in facilitating registration and reporting to the CER, all other project management was being undertaken by RAF. In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10. In forming AgriProve, all soil carbon projects were to be transitioned across to AgriProve. AgriProve then undertook Agency of the projects on behalf of corporate carbon. The process to change project proponent from Corpoate Carbon took 4 years to negotiate the commercial agreements to ensure AgriProve had the ongoing legal right to operate the projects. Whilst the commercial negotiations were taking place, the soil sampling, eligible interst holder consents and preparation of the offsets report(s) were undertaken, in good faith, according to the 2021 Soil Carbon Methodology. Once the project proponent was agreed and transferred, the final variation was the transition to the 2021 Soil Carbon Method under the AgriProve LMS. The CER has been consistently notified and consulated on the 'Legacy' projects, with approvals granted for extenstion of submission to the offsets reports due to the transition from Corporate Carbon to AgriProve 10. engagements.subject: Lead Indicator Assessment positive.
engagements.body: Hi Ella, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is likely worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. I would like to discuss project activities before we mobilise the sampling team. When we speak I would also like to confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas in April? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Quick Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Ella, Yes, the last 5 years are a bit of blur for me too. Regarding the cost of sampling, AgriProve fully covers the cost of all resampling for the life of the project. We follow a fee for success business model which means we only get paid when you do, in the form of a 25% success fee on ACCU issuances. The Soil Carbon Methodology states that a project must have two sampling events within it's first reporting period (5 years). If we are unable to resample before November it may bring the project into question with the regulator. We have not had to test them on this as very few projects are over 5 years old, but there is a chance they would seek to revoke the project. Our position is flexible with what you would like to do with any credits issued, for example if you would rather hold on to them vs. selling on a spot market. However, we would seek compensation for the agreed amount as quoted in the signed commercial terms agreement when the project started. As per the terms, AgriProve would recover the first 750 ACCUs awarded in the event of successful crediting of the project. From our perspective, and regulatory compliance aside, resampling would be worthwhile given the length of time that has past and continued implementation on your part. It would be good to see how the soils may have improved. Can I request that we have a short discussion on what has been done in terms of management change? We would need to link any carbon sequestration to the change in management. Feel free to give me a call on 0401 101 748 at a time that suits. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Ella, Sorry to hear that things have not been going to plan. I completely understand your uncertainty in continuing with the project. From our end - if you are still committed to making these improvements in the long term, we would encourage you to continue with the project. Poor seasons are something that happens in farming and therefore carbon projects, and that is why the contracts are 25 years long. If you are still interested, there is still an opportunity for you to measure an increase and receive ACCU's in the future when you are able to implement your chosen activities. If you would not like to continue, the main thing you need to know is that there will be a fee to repay the Clean Energy Regulators Advanced Payment that was used at the beginning of your project for the baseline sampling. Incoming email — 11 March 2026, 10:00pm AEST From: ella.a@bigpond.com | CC: callum.jay@bigpond.com, will@agriprove.io, djones@agriprove.io Subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions Hi Claudia, We are certain we will not be continuing with AgriProve. While we will continue to implement changes, the past/current seasons, combined with strong evidence for businesses maintaining full ownership of carbon credits rather than selling them through another party, among other factors makes us sure we do not wish to continue. Could you please clarify where in the contract it is stated that the Clean Energy Regulators Advanced Payment has to be repaid? Our reading indicates credits needing to be paid, etc., but can't see a direct reference to this advanced payment and that does contradict our understanding and notes from the time around what risk our business had when setting up the project. Before we seek advice I just want to be clear which sections of the contract are in relation to this repayment being requested. Obviously, as we do not wish to continue with AgriProve if necessary, we will pay. It does confirm our desire to leave either way, as that was not our understanding from our meetings at the start of this project, which indicated a very low financial risk (basically the cost of implementing changes was our input cost) even if we were to opt out at a later date and especially prior to any credits being issued. The advanced payment was discussed with us as a way of reducing costs for all and payments only being made once credits were issued, and there being no financial risk prior to credits being issued. This is in contrast to your email. I understand you were not involved at the start of this project, but we would appreciate your clarification of where in the contract the advanced payment is mentioned. Thank you for your time Regards Ella

engagements.subject: Riverina soils might be worth more than you think
engagements.body: G'Day Jonathan, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural "carbon sink" where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years. Why This Matters for Carbon: The combination of your soil types, pH management and yearly rainfall combination generate a significant carbon opportunity If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? engagements.subject: AgriProve - Farm Visit with Hobbs Margaret
engagements.body: Hi Jon, Thanks for your time with Hobbs yesterday and your interest in exploring soil carbon for The Willows and your other prospective clients with your portfolio. I've attached your HORIZON Snapshot, which shows the estimated opportunity based on our analysis and amended the annual rainfall as rquested. You have 749 eligible hectares across the property, with Chromosol soils that create conditions suited to carbon building under improved management. The analysis shows Strength Zones scattered across the western paddocks, through the northern sections, and across the southern and eastern blocks where modeled carbon levels currently sit above the property median, and Opportunity Zones prominent across the northern paddocks and through central sections where targeted grazing management could support carbon gains. With 650mm of rainfall and soil depths reaching 2.1m across extensive areas, there's substantial capacity for carbon storage in the soil profile. The 82% eligibility rate is strong—satellite analysis excluded forests, infrastructure, and waterways, leaving 749 hectares of project-ready grazing land across your 911-hectare property. We're projecting approximately 56,175 ACCUs over 25 years based on our rainfall band methodology. At 749 eligible hectares, Growth Farms is well-positioned for two efficiently scaled projects (~400ha each). You're situated in a highly active region—approximately 40 neighboring properties across the Wagga Wagga-Tumut corridor are at various project stages, and credited projects within 50km are actively receiving credits, demonstrating these conditions support carbon building. Next steps will be focused on a tailored Land Management Strategy Call which is approx. 45 minutes to understand the properties history, current practices and how you would like to implement improved soil health practice with the intention of undertaking a soil carbon project with AgriProve. So we can arrange baseline soil sampling prior to Autumn, it would be great to lock in a time for the Land Management Strategy Call next week. Below is a link to schedule a time for this call. 60 min, 30 min, and 15 min meeting: https://meetings-ap1.hubspot.com/ben2218 If you have any questions, let me know and I'll touch base with you before the end of the week. engagements.body: Morning Jon, I hope you had a good weekend. We are now reading to issue you the Key Commercial Terms and Carbon Project Plan for Weatherall Carbon Project. Before I do so, I wanted to give you a heads up on a couple of things happening on our end before it lands with you. From 1 July, we're moving to a new mandatory baseline sampling configuration — 24 cores per Carbon Estimation Area, up from the current 12. This comes out of recent independent review work and improves project accuracy and reduces variance, so it's a sound change. But it does affect cost. At current per-core pricing, the difference looks like this: Current configuration (16 cores): ~$8,000 per CEA New configuration from 1 July (24 cores): ~$10,770 per CEA For anyone who has signed their Key Commercial Terms before 30 June, current pricing applies to their baselining. The original Weatherall HORIZON report quote was $12,608 which aligns with the standard 4x4 config for 2 projects. If we expand the number of cores to 6 per strata, the baseline cost becomes $17,664. The second thing worth flagging — if your property is in New South Wales, particularly the Riverina region, our sampling crew will be on the ground in May and June. If we can tie your baselining into that window, we can lock in a guaranteed date. After that, we genuinely can't say when we'll next be back in the region based on sampler availability and weather conditions — it could be 12 months away, which would push your first crediting cycle out accordingly. I'd rather you have the full picture now than find out later. Happy to run through what it means for your specific property if that's useful — just let me know a time that suits. engagements.body: Good Afternoon Ella, Sorry to hear that things have not been going to plan. I completely understand your uncertainty in continuing with the project. From our end - if you are still committed to making these improvements in the long term, we would encourage you to continue with the project. Poor seasons are something that happens in farming and therefore carbon projects, and that is why the contracts are 25 years long. If you are still interested, there is still an opportunity for you to measure an increase and receive ACCU's in the future when you are able to implement your chosen activities. If you would not like to continue, the main thing you need to know is that there will be a fee to repay the Clean Energy Regulators Advanced Payment that was used at the beginning of your project for the baseline sampling. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Hi Claudia, We are certain we will not be continuing with agriprove. While we will continue to implement changes, the past/current seasons, combined with strong evidence for businesses maintaining full ownership of carbon credits rather than selling them through another party, among other factors makes us sure we do not wish to continue. Could you please clarify where in the contract it is stated that the Clean Energy Regulators Advanced Payment has to be repaid? Our reading indicates credits needing to be paid, etc., but can't see a direct reference to this advanced payment and that does contradict our understanding and notes from the time around what risk our business had when setting up the project. Before we seek advice I just want to be clear which sections of the contract are in relation to this repayment being request. Obviously, as we do not wish to continue with agriprove if necessary, we will pay. It does confirm our desire to leave either way, as that was not our understanding from our meetings at the start of this project, which indicated a very low financial risk (basically the cost of implementing changes was our input cost) even if we were to opt out at a later date and especially prior to any credits being issued. The advanced payment was discussed with us as a way of reducing costs for all and payments only being made once credits were issued, and there being no financial risk prior to credits being issued. This is in contrast to your email, I understand you were not involved at the start of this project, but we would appreciate your clarification of where in the contract the advanced payment is mentioned. engagements.subject: AgriProve community meeting
engagements.body: Good morning Mike, I hope you are all well! AgriProve is excited to invite you to join us in Colosseum at Kylie and Lance Stephenson’s property for an AgriProve community event. A big thank you to Kylie and Lance for hosting the occasion! The event will be held on Wednesday 22nd of November at 1142 Blackmans Gap Road, Colosseum. Kick off will be at 10am, finishing at approximately 2pm. The days agenda: Morning Presentations: 10am – 12:00pm The morning will be a chance to learn about some of AgriProve’s new initiatives. Learn about the new opportunity to integrate cattle monitoring with your AgriProve soil carbon project and find out about the new reef credit opportunities upcoming through the Reef Credits: Grazing Land Management method, developed in partnership with Verterra and Greencollar. We are also excited to have a presentation from our keynote speaker, Mr Hobbs Magaret, coming all the way from the USA. Hobbs is a rancher from east Texas, founder of Sisters Cattle Co. and an expert in using ultra-high density grazing to maximise carbon drawdown and production efficiency. BBQ Lunch: 12:00 – 12:45 Following presentations there will be a chance to unwind with BBQ lunch and refreshments provided. Afternoon Farm Tour: 12:45 – 2:00pm To wrap up the day we will all head out for a farm tour led by Lance and Kylie to see what they are focusing on currently. It will also be an opportunity for everyone share stories about what has worked for them. If you are able to make it, we would love to see you there for what will be a great opportunity to meet others, share knowledge and a bite to eat. Please accept this invitation as soon as possible to RSVP. This will help us get an idea of numbers ahead of time. For any dietary requirements or if any family and friends would like to attend, we would love them to. Please simply notify us in advance at william@agriprove.io or team@agriprove.io. Kind regards, Team at AgriProve

engagements.subject: Request to resample Pearce Carbon Project
engagements.body: You don't often get email from mmoller57@gmail.com. Learn why this is important Hi Barbara, ok for you to sample again, however it has been very dry over the past six to nine months, so I’m not sure that there will have been any significant increase in soil carbon since you last sampled in May 2023. There has been over 100 mm of rain in the last couple of weeks, but I’m still not sure that this will have caused an increase in soil carbon. Regards Mike On Wednesday, 6 December 2023, AgriProve > wrote: Hi Mike, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator, there are many other factors that can influence sequestration that does not guarantee soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. Can you please confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas within the period of 18th to 22nd December 2023? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions, please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Pearce Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Michael, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have been going on the ground of your project, I will attempt to contact you in the coming days on your mobile. On this call I will confirm that you are happy to go ahead with re-sampling your project. Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. engagements.subject: Deforestation-free Beef Credential
engagements.body: Good afternoon Michael, Thank you for your request for a Deforestation-Free Beef Credential! We at AgriProve are excited to assist your business in ensuring you are at the front of the line to access premium supply chains. We are proud to work together with innovative producers such as yourself to showcase the exemplary management Aussie farmers are globally renown for! How the process will work from here: You complete the attached invoice payment. AgriProve and Verterra complete a full retrospective geospatial analysis to validate your property as compliant with EU, international, and domestic beef purchaser requirements. We provide you with a 3rd party verified, shareable report and a profile badge in your AgriProve platform. You are then able to share this with any interested buyers, banks, or insurers as proof that you are managing in a sustainable manner. If you would like any more information on the credential please feel free to read about it on the Knowledgebase here: Why is it important to have a Deforestation-Free Beef Credential?: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-the-deforestation-free-beef-credential. Once again - thank you for partnering with AgriProve, we are honoured to assist your enterprise in articulating your management to the market. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions. engagements.body: Hi Michael, Will Frecheville from AgriProve. I have just tried to call you regarding the Pearce CP. engagements.subject: Re: Pearce CP - Project Continuance.
engagements.body: Thanks Will, I am presently in Cambodia so generally not answering phone calls unless I recognise the number, due to roaming charges. I am a bit surprised that the soil carbon levels have decreased, not sure what's happening there. My recollection is that the samples were taken around April 2025, so if they weren't tested until August 2025 that does seem to be a bit of a delay, not sure if a delay in testing can cause decreases in soil carbon due to microbial activity? Re the property, groundcover is generally well maintained and the seasons over the past couple of years have been on the wet side, so I thought with the wet season spelling and the paddock rotations that have been happening, soil carbon should at least be maintained, if not increased. So at this stage I am inclined not to proceed any further with the project, seeing as there has been no increase in measured soil carbon over the past 4.5 to 5 years. I will be back in Australia after 20 February 2026 so if you wanted to discuss this on or after 23 February that would be fine. If you are able to contact me via whatsapp that would be fine also, we just need to take account of the three or four hour time difference (9 am here in Cambodia is midday in Qld, 1 pm in NSW/Vic, your call this morning came through at 6.48 am Siem Reap time) and I need to have access to wifi, which I have most of the time (11.30 am to 7.30 pm Qld time). engagements.subject: Grazing Management Changes and Timeline
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Thanks for your time just before, as discussed, the CER has asked about the grazing practice changes you have made. Specifically, the first water upgrades in 2021, and some sub-divisions of paddocks. engagements.subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. From: Jeff Bell Sent: Sunday, 2 February 2025 2:55 PM To: Dylan Jones Subject: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Dylan, The Agriprove platform said "Generate income through a Reef Credit project Your property is eligible to undertake a Reef Credit Project." Is this correct or is it just that we are geographically eligible? Can a reef credit project co-exist with a carbon project? I have been looking into "natural sequence farming" which is all about keeping water and dissolved nutrients on farm through modifying existing contour drains and/or constructing level contours.(which fits neatly into what the "reef credit project" would be looking to achieve. Attended a "natural sequence farming" field day yesterday and there was so much that explained why areas of our farm have limited performance compared to the mean. If we spend money on training and earthworks to keep more water and nutrients on our farm(approx 94 % of which is under a carbon project) would we be eligible for a "reef credit project"? Jeff Bell

engagements.subject: Re: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Definitely would not be grazing management as that is already done. It would be remedial earth works to modify the existing drain contours and where needed construct new contours to slow the flow of water and nutrients and keep both on farm rather than running off down the waterway which does come in the list of gully management methodology activities. Most of the farm can benefit from this in productivity(and consequently carbon sequestration) but only about 30 percent of the farm(my guestimate) has substandard ground cover which in my opinion could release some sediment and nutrients off farm. My take is that the amount of sediment lost from the farm in its current condition would be to low to bother with. The only place where there would be any amount would be a bit hard to manage as it comes pouring through from next door in a water way only a couple of hundred metres from our bottom fence. If Agriprove think there is anything worth pursuing then I will think about it. I myself think not but that is an opinion not based on knowledge. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jeff, I have just completed your yearly satellite assessment for your carbon project. As you know we use this as an indicator for if we think resampling would be worthwhile. Your assessment this year ( attached) has shown an increase in the average NDRE from baseline to current period and an increase in the past year. This indicates that re-sampling this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration. This does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We need to complete the physical sampling to know what is happening in the ground. Next steps: Before we schedule the resampling date, we need to complete the phone call section of the review. Is there a time next week that would suit to do that? I have some prep I need to do before the call so locking in a time in advance works best. If you have any questions please let me know. Talk soon. engagements.body: Good Moring Jeff, Yeah it is completely possible for us to do that. Do you know exactly what tests you want done? For an idea of potential price and difference tests I have attached an example of a quote we got for someone else and the full price list. Keeping in mind this is an older one and they may have changed since then. I had a look at your project, and you have 9 sample sites. You would see that on your results in the past you have 18 because they test the top layer (0-30cm) and then a deeper piece of that sample ( 30-100cm). If you wanted to do both depths, you would need to pay for 18 samples. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Strategy Call
engagements.body: Hi Katie, Thank you for booking a soil carbon project strategy meeting. This meeting will cover: 1. Select the property boundaries on your soil carbon project. 2. Define the eligible activities you will be implementing on your project. 3. Provide a walkthrough of the Land Management Strategy and the Consent to Register and Commitment to Implement Document (CTR-CTI) 4. Answer any additional questions that you have since our first meeting. We also need to collate historical farm records (5 years), so please have the following information on hand: Lot and plan number for the property General nutrient and mineral applications Any pasture renovation information including species composition and hectares planted each year Approximate yearly livestock stocking rates, Any cropping information (grain, seed, and horticulture) including hectares planted, type, and yield. Need to make changes? engagements.subject: RE: Soil carbon project progress update
engagements.body: Dear Katie and Christian, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. I'll give you a call to makes sure you received my email and should you have any questions or need assistance, don’t hesitate to reach out.
