engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Christophe, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? See my link below. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Christophe, I have chased up your results and attached them to this email. Sorry that there was such a delay on getting them to you. For future, something to be aware of is all of the results automatically go into our online platform where you can see them in there as soon as they are ready. I have checked and you do have an account already set up. As you will see, there has not been a measured increase in soil carbon in this sampling round. While this may be disappointing, it is important to remember that soil carbon projects are a long-term investment, with increase in SOC often taking a long time to be achieved. For next steps: * If you would like to discuss your results and how the math's works I can book you in a call with Will who is the guru on that side of things. * We have a grazier in residence who is available to chat with you about grazing practices and what you can do to increase carbon. * I am working through the 5 year reporting side of things for you with the operations team. We can also book in a time to chat with you and your neighbors to go through HORIZON- are you looking to chat to someone about how horizon works and the layers or more of the practical implementation of it ? Let me know what your looking for and I can arrange the best person to talk too. engagements.subject: Trophy CP (CRD207716) [SEC=OFFICIAL]
engagements.body: OFFICIAL Regarding the Trophy CP (CRD207716), we have identified a few matters in the crediting application. 1. The LMS states that the project proposes to undertake three activities: application of nutrients, re‑establishment of pasture, and alteration of the stocking rate. It is unclear what activities have been undertaken during the reporting period. The Executive Summary indicates that only re‑establishment of pasture and alteration of the stocking rate were completed, however the summary in the Offsets Report states that all three proposed activities have been undertaken. Could you please confirm which version is correct, noting that there is minimal information in the Executive Summary regarding the application of nutrients in the project area? If only two of the three activities have been implemented to date, could you clarify whether the landholder intends to implement all three activities over the project period, or only the two described in the Executive Summary? Please provide this information by the 10th of February 2026. 1. Emissions from maiden ewes (output of equation 15) were not included in the livestock emission calculations (equation 12), and it is unclear whether maiden ewes (and breeding ewes) were present during the baseline period. It is noted that maiden and breeding ewes were present during the reporting period. * Synthetic fertiliser emissions: The incorrect emissions factor in equation 19 was applied for both the baseline and reporting periods. The Queensland value for cotton was used (2.59) instead of the Victoria value for non‑irrigated pasture (1.72). * Baseline and reporting periods: Livestock emissions appear to have been reported over six years rather than five years over both periods; in particular, 365 days were applied to each year during the baseline period. engagements.subject: AgriProve Carbon Farming - Important links provided with next steps
engagements.body: Hi Leesa, Boyd and Michelle, Thanks again for our time last week, really appreciate the opportunity to discuss the potential of a soil carbon project with AgriProve. Below are a few of the links to that we discussed which will be useful to continue the conversation relating to the potential of a soil carbon project: Horizon (link provided, click here to view): https://agriprove.io/in-the-news-old/mr-wsd-horizon-launch As mentioned on our call, Horizon is a highly sophisticated, machine learning soil organic carbon model which is providing farmers unprecedented visibility into soil carbon, access to annual crediting cycles and unlocking a new era of data-driven farm profitability. Horizon webinar (link provided, click here to view): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bv_GcFnJGTg which was conducted late last year with over 180 registered attendees. This was great insight into what Horizon is and how it delivers monthly soil carbon insights and annual credit issuance to current and future registered projects. AgriProve Project Proposal: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0xGt-0 which covers the questions that I can take you through as part of your tailored Land Management Strategy Call which are essentially the next steps in the process to ensure we are on the way to developing your Carbon Project Plan. This is the 45 minute call that I mentioned in our meeting last week. AgriProve Project Proposal - Farm Management.pdf: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0xGw-0 which also formulates part of your tailored Carbon Project Plan. This document is to be filled in by Michelle and Boyd prior to confirming a time to go through the Land Management Strategy Call. AgriProve Case Studies (link provided, click here to view): https://agriprove.io/casestudies If there is anything else you need from me or Will, please don't hesitate to let either of us know and we'd be happy to support any questions moving forward. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve Carbon Farming - Important links provided with next steps
engagements.body: Hi Michelle, I hope you and Boyd are well and that the week has started well for you. I wanted to follow up on our land management strategy call from January 29th. We're making great progress with your project documentation, but I'm still waiting on a few key pieces of information before I can submit everything to our operations team. Outstanding Items: Project Name – We discussed this during our call, and you mentioned checking with Leesa about whether it should align with your grant funding. Have you had a chance to settle on a name? (Could be as simple as "Tansey Pastoral" or "Armstrong Creek", or something more creative!) Stocking Rate Details – You mentioned you have this information on hand but needed to pull it together. Specifically, I need: Current and historical stocking rates (DSE/LSU/AE per hectare) Duration of grazing periods Number of paddocks and their sizes/average size Rest and recovery periods Five-Year Farm Management History – This includes both the grazing history document and the horticultural management section (for your 19-hectare pecan orchard) Click here for the link to AgriProve Project Proposal - Farm Management.pdf: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0zt0n0 Paddock Maps – These will help us with the mapping phase and understanding the boundaries for both your grazing and horticultural areas Land Title Confirmation – You were going to double-check which title the potential pivot irrigation would fall under (once confirmed) Once I receive these details, I'll finalize the land management strategy document and submit it to Will's operations team to develop your carbon project plan with the intent to register the project. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or need clarification on any of these items. I'm here to help! On another note, our Head of Operations, Will Frecheville, is potentially available for a farm visit the week of February 23rd. This could be a great opportunity to walk through your property together, discuss your eligible activities in more detail, and answer any questions you might have. Let me know if you and Boyd would be interested and what day that week might work best for you. Looking forward to hearing from you. Cheers, Ben Ben Payne | Account Manager Phone: 1300 467 645: tel:{Phone} Mobile: 0403893668: tel:{Mobile} Email: ben@agriprove.io: mailto:{E-mail} Address: 1/601 Dean Street, Albury NSW 2640 www.agriprove.io: https://agriprove.io/ : https://www.linkedin.com/company/agriprove-pty-ltd/ : https://www.facebook.com/agriprove1/ : https://www.twitter.com/agriprove : https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCj6-LPG2-c5h5RUn5u8SuZw Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.body: Hey Dan, We haven't met, my name is Harry and I head up Growth for AgriProve - I just got off the phone to Bill and he mentioned you were keen to explore the potential of a soil carbon project. If you want a clear, data-backed view of your property’s carbon opportunity, we can provide a complimentary, tailored soil carbon report. This assessment will: Map eligible areas under ERF criteria, excluding remnant vegetation, waterways, infrastructure, or steep terrain. Assess soil type, clay content, and depth to estimate carbon storage potential and long-term stability. Review rainfall and climate to identify where pasture growth and groundcover support soil carbon accumulation. Highlight land management potential, showing where improved grazing could drive measurable carbon outcomes and long-term value. engagements.subject: AgriProve x Brunham Grazing - Soil Carbon Report
engagements.body: Hey Dan, Please find attached a desktop Soil Carbon Report for Burnham Grazing - There is some really strong potential for a soil carbon project as you were probably already aware and my project size estimations come in a little larger than previously estimated. Apologies again for the delay - as requested I was looking into the additional potential of a Reef Credit project and had some slow responses from our partners. engagements.subject: Re: Soil Carbon Proposal Plan - Update
engagements.body: Hi Dan, I hope you're well. As an FYI - we will be likely moving to a more regular position where all of our landholders and partners will be required to have their own ANREU account to hold their ACCUs (this is the same set up Adam Gunthorpe has for his ACCU's essentially) Setting up an ANREU account can be done via the CER's website; or we can do it on behalf of the landholder once your Key Commercial Terms have bene signed. https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance What this means, is we have a number of marking positives and offerings that can be put to the landholder. We can absolutely set up an ANREU account for you Landholder has full flexibility and autonomy of their ACCUs You can elect to sell either through AgriProve or on their own, or through another broker This avoids a brokerage fee or holding fee from AgriProve if they have their ACCUs transferred and broker through someone else. We will look for formalise a process for setting up these accounts, starting with our landholders who have already been issued credits, and then working through clients with a measured increase and then onto clients as a part of their onboarding/re-sampling. Dear SCIG Members, This is a placeholder for an opportunity to explore soil carbon issues in early drafting of the Integrated Farm and Land Management Method under the Australian ACCU Scheme. Our input here will be fed through the Carbon Market Institute IFLM Taskforce. It will also help us explore and develop SCIG positions on IFLM method issues. For context, the government has agreed to continue to develop the IFLM with the ERAC (Emissions Reduction Advisory Committee) in the interim as the Chubb Review recommendations particularly the CAIC (Carbon Abatement Integrity Committee) are implemented and established. Method Development Interim Framework (dcceew.gov.au) You might like to share this opportunity a little wider within your company with people experienced in method development. Within SCIG I will develop a ‘tag’ for contacts who can help with method issues. People who attend from your companies can be added to this list. engagements.body: Dear Members, Agenda 1)Agriculture and Land Sectoral strategy response - ComPAC 2) FinMeRC proposal of SCIG membership strategy Our operating environment as an industry is likely to be significantly shaped by the government’s developing Agriculture and Land Sectoral Strategy. This is a placeholder for a meeting to refine Soil Carbon Industry input as below. A draft response for your consideration will be circulated in advance. engagements.subject: RE: Meeting wIth Agriprove and RAF: Summary Points
engagements.body: Hi Deane, Some comments below: 1. We will amend and restate (ie replace) the current agreements between Corporate Carbon and the farmers and Corporate Carbon and RAF (“New Agreements”) - Agreed; new agreements also to replace Corporate Carbon with AgriProve. 2. The New Agreements will limit the application of the Projects to the contracted based-line trial areas (~10% of the total farm areas) - Agreed; new agreements will only relate to the registered project areas. All cases have now had area variations lodged and approved by the CER to limit the registered projects to the baselined area. 3. Similarly Corporate Carbon will remove any wording relating to ownership or rights over the Farmer’s soil carbon as currently appearing in the Participation Deed - Agreed; any reference to claim on ownership on landholders soil carbon will be removed. 4. The Farmers and RAF shall receive their respective proportion of verified ACCUs (following completion of the audit process) for T0-T1 (first 5 years) into their own ANREU accounts, to sell on the secondary market, hold as carbon offsets or otherwise, based on initial splits assuming ~$12/ACCU: a. 66.5% Farmers Agreed; 66.5% of ACCUs to landholder. Landholders are individually responsible for establishing ANREU accounts. b. 25% RAF c. 8.5% Agriprove (for them to deal with as they see fit) - Points b and c pertaining to the remaining 33.5% to be agreed between RAF and AgriProve based on work completed to date (refer to the attached spreadsheet) and CAC servicing obligations. 5. ACCUs generated and verified for T1-T2 (next 5 years of which we are already 2-3 years into) will be received by farmers into their own ANREU accounts in a proportion of 72.5-75%. The balance will be split between Agriprove and RAF which shall be determined following a clear and agreed definition of the respective roles and responsibilities of Agriprove and RAF for T1 -T2; this will occur during May. Farmers will deal solely with RAF (as the ‘Agent’) but some services may be provided by Agriprove to RAF. The details of the service and % allocation will be shared with farmers - Agreed in principle; please see attached breakdown of tasks and responsibilities for further discussion between RAF/AgriProve. 6. All audit costs for ACCU verification shall be borne by the individual farmers - Agreed; the audit process will be managed by AgriProve and audit quotes provided to RAF for approval with landholders before progressing. 7. Following the conclusion of T2 and for T3 and beyond (at completion of 10 year ERF contract period plus), Agriprove will exit the Projects and the farmers will become their own project Proponents under regulation and RAF shall be appointed as Project Agents. At this time, the splits may be renegotiated between Farmers and RAF - Agreed; AgriProve to be removed as Proponent at year 10 and replaced with landholder, RAF to be registered as Agent. AgriProve have no further involvement in the projects after the proponent has been varied. 8. Upon acceptance of the ’New Agreements’ by all parties, the following steps will be undertaken prior to ACCU creation: a. The Novation of Project Proponent transferring from Corporate Carbon Australia to AgriProve; Agreed; AgriProve to manage proponency variation process once agreements are signed and AgriProve has legal right to do so. Note the assessment period can be a minimum of 3 months at the CER and we cannot initiate audit until this variation is approved. b. Auditing of the Offsets Report; Agreed; AgriProve to manage this process. Noting that proponent and method variations need to be lodged and approved by the CER once AgriProve has legal right; it may take up to 6 months before these variations are approved. c. Completion and submission of the Offsets Report (aligned to 2021 Methodology) to the Regulator; Agreed; AgriProve to manage this process, refer to the point above. d. Setup of respective ANREU accounts for Farmers and RAF; Agreed; This is to be manage…

engagements.subject: Re: Meeting wIth Agriprove and RAF: Summary Points to Progress Project Agreements
engagements.body: Dear Kieren, My apologies for being hard to contact over the last 10 days (been in Africa). Below is a summary our collective position. We refer to our letter dated 3 April 2024 and our meeting dated 2 May 2024. As per the meeting, all splits for T0-T1 were to remain as per the original contract being: a. 66.5% Farmers Agreed; 66.5% of ACCUs to landholder. Landholders are individually responsible for establishing ANREU accounts. b. 25% RAF c. 8.5% Agriprove (for them to deal with as they see fit) If Corporate Carbon believes that it is entitled to compensation for any additional tasks or previously nominated/agreed RAF tasks that it performed during this period, then it should specify these tasks and invoice for them based on a market time-cost recovery rate. For T1-T2, RAF is prepared to accept a revenue split proportionate to the indicative roles and responsibilities suggested in your spreadsheet. RAF does not however believe that this equates to 50%/50% on the remaining non-landholder ACCUs, specifically the 25% RAF portion. The monetisation of this (@$32/ACCU) will far exceed the original 8.5% split (@$10/ACCU) - assuming the carbon price is projected to exceed $80/ACCU by 2030. Therefore, Agriprove is already making a substantial uplift. We may be prepared to move down from 25% and lift Agriprove up from 8.5%, but we need to analyse the spreadsheet and agree proportional roles, responsibilities and benefit. We are available to do this at your convenience. If this approach is acceptable, let’s organise a call next week and please prepare new restated agreement for our review, amendment (if required) and approval based on the above and the below agreed points (subject to T1-T2 splits); this should demonstrate to the Regulator that we are progressing these projects as a matter of priority. If this is not acceptable, based on legal advice, RAF and the Farmers shall terminate its arrangement with Corporate Carbon for breach of contract. However we trust that this provides the basis for a mutually 'shared benefit' arrangement to be struck. Regards Regards Deane Belfield Director Regenerative Australian Farmers (soil carbon project developers) ￼ Winner Leadership Award - National Carbon Cocky Awards E: deane@regenfarmers.com.au W: www.regenfarmers.com.au M: 0414 v617542

engagements.subject: SCIG Summit - Agreeing on objectives.
engagements.body: Updating with notes from SCIG meeting today. Dear SCIG Members, One outcome from the ‘Listening tour’ of members was that we would appreciate getting together for a Summit. This meeting will cover Agenda Agreement on objectives for a SCIG Summit (drafted below) Scoping a date for a Soil Carbon Summit (proposed April/May 2025) Formation of a SCIG Summit committee. Hamish, Louisa, Phil Mulvey – Tours co-ordinator, Louise – WA liaison [charter jet 😊 ], Oli - AgriFutures, Zoe Program committee - TBC Scientific presentations lead - Zoe, Ben, Soil Science Australia Working committee – Hamish to lead on site in Dubbo In RSVP’ing please either indicate ‘Yes’ you will attend, let us know your delegate and that they will attend email myself, Hamish Webb or Louisa Kiely an apology and an indication of your company’s ability to support a SCIG Summit next year. DRAFT SCIG Summit Objectives Need a headline GOAL SUGGESTED HEADER: The Soil Carbon Industry Group announces the Second Australasian Soil Carbon Summit BYLINE: Expanding opportunity, showcasing success, on farm productivity gains. – Expanding opportunity, - Farmers decarbonising the atmosphere - Showing success on the farm - on farm productivity gains Teir 1 Objectives (in order of priority) Engage Farmers - To engage and connect with as many farmers as possible who would like to learn more about soil carbon and meet with SCIG members Cross pollination node for discussion across the value chain with developers and regulators and markets Share Case Studies - To openly share success stories (and challenges faced) in the soil carbon industry Platform for Science and Innovation - To hear from scientific developments and innovation successes in soil carbon. engagements.body: Dear Stuart, My general comments regarding the agreements are as follows: 1. Deed of Novation 1. This needs to be a Deed of Novation “AND VARIATION”, to accommodate the changes 2. I understand that this is a template, and that this revision is in respect of each of the ACCU Sales Agreements with each Seller 3. Clause 1.3 - All definitions of the Original Agreement should be retained and those clauses also with the Novation and Variation Agreement taking precedence to the extent of any inconsistency - 4. Clause 2.2 – Agreement is “varied” and (a) – Annexure “2” not “B”; 5. Clause 6.6 and 6.10 of the Original Agreement needs to be varied as the farmer’s proportions of ACCU’s will be vested in farmers own registry accounts, balance will go into RAF and Agriprove accounts 6. “Price” is no longer defined in the Transaction Particulars and should be replaced with “Percentages” as per the agreed T0-T1 and T1 -T2 splits, and definition of Surplus ACCU’s should be deleted 7. We need to define the T0-T1 and T1 -T2 period and exclude T2-T3 as per agreed position (no relationship post T2 end) 8. Need to await description of titles in Annexure 2 and 3 to ensure reserved to “trial baseline areas” 9. Where is the $5k cap on Buyer services charges? 10. We need reference to “No ownership rights over Seller’s Soil Carbon” as per the agreement 11. All other agreements other than the ACCU Sales and Agreements and the ERF Participation Deed mentioned in the attached letter need to be terminated 12. I will defer to Deane regarding breakdown of T2 responsibilities (assume this is as per previous spreadsheet) I can make these amendments if necessary but please note that the costs of my review and amendments are to be covered by Agriprove, as per our previous agreement. 1. Soil ERF Participation Deed 1. Replace ERF with ACCU scheme throughout 2. Delete clause 2.1(3) as Proponent will be issued its proportion to satisfy ERF requirements (unless I am missing something?) engagements.body: Dear Simon, We have updated the Deed of Novation and ERF Participation Deed as requested referencing answers to your comments below: 1. Deed of Novation 1. This needs to be a Deed of Novation “AND VARIATION”, to accommodate the changes - Complete 2. I understand that this is a template, and that this revision is in respect of each of the ACCU Sales Agreements with each Seller – no action 3. Clause 1.3 - All definitions of the Original Agreement should be retained and those clauses also with the Novation and Variation Agreement taking precedence to the extent of any inconsistency – Complete 4. Clause 2.2 – Agreement is “varied” and (a) – Annexure “2” not “B”; - Complete Clause 6.6 and 6.10 of the Original Agreement needs to be varied as the farmer’s proportions of ACCU’s will be vested in farmers own registry accounts, balance will go into RAF and AgriProve accounts - Clause 2.2(e) specifies the percentages of ACCUs to be distributed in place of Schedule 1 of the Original Agreement. 1. “Price” is no longer defined in the Transaction Particulars and should be replaced with “Percentages” as per the agreed T0-T1 and T1 -T2 splits, and definition of Surplus ACCU’s should be deleted – Complete 2. We need to define the T0-T1 and T1 -T2 period and exclude T2-T3 as per agreed position (no relationship post T2 end) – Complete 3. Need to await description of titles in Annexure 2 and 3 to ensure reserved to “trial baseline areas” – Acknowledged, once the ‘template’ novation and variation deed, ACCU Scheme Participation Deed, and Varied ACCU Sales and Licence Agreement are approved, each project will have updates to the particulars for each landholder and project. 4. Where is the $5k cap on Buyer services charges? – not relevant. Any agreed services cap between landholders and RAF is separate to this. AgriProve is not party to that. If you are referring to the $5,00 per project ($25,000 total) agreed payment for work performed AgriProve will invoice RAF for this amount, not the landholders as previously agreed. 5. We need reference to “No ownership rights over Seller’s Soil Carbon” as per the agreement – there is no reference to having rights to the Seller’s soil carbon therefore this is not necessary 6. All other agreements other than the ACCU Sales and Agreements and the ERF Participation Deed mentioned in the attached letter need to be terminated – This is covered by Clause 8.7 of the Novation and Variation Deed. All agreements between the outgoing party and the incoming party and the landholders will follow this agreement. 7. I will defer to Deane regarding breakdown of T2 responsibilities (assume this is as per previous spreadsheet) – yes. Not part of this process with landholders. I can make these amendments if necessary but please note that the costs of my review and amendments are to be covered by AgriProve, as per our previous agreement. No previous agreement was made. Each party is responsible for their own legal costs. 1. Soil ERF Participation Deed 1. Replace ERF with ACCU scheme throughout - Complete 2. Delete clause 2.1(3) as Proponent will be issued its proportion to satisfy ERF requirements (unless I am missing something?) – the nominated registry account is issued all project ACCUs which are then transferred within 10 business days. From a functional perspective, it is the requirement of the CER and in the CFI Act, that the Project’s nominated registry account is where project ACCUs will be issued. This is where all ACCUs are issued. The CER does not have the capacity or capability to issue ACCUs to multiple registry accounts. From: Harry Clark Sent: Tuesday, June 11, 2024 9:34 AM To: Dylan Jones Cc: Duncan Farquhar Subject: Lyndon Hunt - Lawrence CP Good Morning DJ, Just providing an update on the Lawrence project, after we noted a RFI on the eligible activity. Originally, we had planned to use the mineral deficiency aspect as the eligible activity, but we have not yet taken soil tests, nor does Lyndon have much budget to purchase more than bare minimum fertiliser this year. Lyndon is however implementing a legume-based cover crop every second year into the program. Historically, he was cropping in one year, and then resting as fallow in the second year, so he will now be doing the cropping program for 1 year and a legume cover crop in the second year instead of the fallow. discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Discussion around Greenhams certification. Notes below: Looking at Greenhams 'Never Ever' Greenhams - 10c premium per kg - $32 per animal Needs to be higher Need to reward early adopters with a bigger reward - $100 a head / $0.30 per kg Co-benefit of being in a carbon projects Don’t want to be a price taker, being a price maker - put the responsibly How do you get into the exclusive club - rare air - rewarding those who follow the process especially Something juicy you can hang your hat on Marketing cattle through $0.30 premium market - on 100 head it's $10,000 There is not enough money in it to keep re-investing in it - with a yearly benefit makes it worth it to keep the practices going Adopting a philosophy with the carbon project and then it becomes Delayed return to drip feed of annual return through the premium Market needs to head this way if you want uptake Consensus is for 10c they don't give a shit MSA graded to 57-61 (eating quality) Marble score 6+ - carbon premium Deep dive into the marble scoring Story is the most important thing - don't sell the story short Farmers are terrible story tellers Let the farmer tell the story about the climate aspect Go down and deep dive on premium branded meat for sale and look at the story of never ever, great southern, little joe, maccas beef Tier 1 - in it (carbon project) Tier 2 - generating carbon (baby Dylan has f Get JC and someone else to round-table with us Complete against eating quality with good and validated story - government taking full control Do the practice change (which is hard) and get rewarded and paid more Let the carbon cattle enter a premium market with the branded story Going to have a meeting in 10 days in Singapore Regen farmers and the story telling - paddock to plate regen product How do we put the AgriProve validated branding out there - already have the validation process Environmentally friendly - touch hearts and souls about the premium product - unique and nothing that anyone else can offer Something that catches your eye in a meat cooler Eco-credits - we need to look into it

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Discussion around Greenhams certification and the criteria they needed. Sent him EOS imagery and gave him account for Crop Monitoring as an observer Vegetation score - groundcover Kg of carbon emitted/kg of weight gain

Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.subject: Sustainability certification questions
engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.body: Hi Dylan, I will look into this in the coming weeks. From our perspective, the first thing we will need to consider is whether we continue with the projects. Should we continue, I will address your other questions and requests. Cheers Paul McDougall Manager - Natural Capital Paraway Pastoral Company Limited 70 McNamara Street | PO Box 22, Orange NSW 2800 M: 0414 344 464 paul.mcdougall@paraway.com.au www.paraway.com.au [cid:image007.jpg@01DB7942.4B0765A0] From: Dylan Jones Sent: Tuesday, 7 January 2025 2:17 PM To: Paul McDougall Subject: [EXT] AgriProve - Steam Plains / Perry's Paddock Carbon Projects Caution: This is an email from an external source. Please take care when clicking on links or opening attachments. Hi Paul, Thanks for speaking with me earlier. Providing an update for you to get you up to speed on the status of the soil carbon projects. Let's pick this up again when you return from leave late Jan. As they stand, no commercial agreement was put in place between Paraway and AgriProve, so we'd want to come to some formal arrangement moving forward. I believe there had been some past discussions around the 25% AgriProve success fee on future ACCUs, and Paraway seeking to retain 100% of ACCU issuances. We are happy to come to an agreement there, the only consideration would be that the projects have entered their 5th year of existence and would therefore be due to be externally audited at the end of their first reporting period (5 years). We would ask that a commercial agreement that establishes AgriProve has the legal right to operate the projects on the landholder's behalf be in place prior to August 2025. The carbon projects were declared conditionally by the Clean Energy Regulator, meaning the consent of each relevant interest-holder to the existence of the project must be obtained before the end of the first reporting period. In this case, we would seek the signatures of two current directors of the following entities: Registered Proprietor: Macquarie Agricultural Funds Management No.2 Pty Limited (ACN: 611 566 217) Mortgagee: National Australia Bank Leasee: Paraway Pastoral Company Ltd AgriProve will work through the process of obtaining these signatures in due course with your assistance if required. Both the Perry's Paddock and Steam Plains Carbon Projects exhibit positive trends in their satellite-derived NDRE data indicators since the projects were baselined in 2020. This suggests it would be worthwhile resampling the projects to obtain another round of soil data to compare their respective carbon stocks. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project's registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project’s registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Mitch, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: HI Mitch, No Worries. I will check in with Geoff about where Beale and Cooper are up to. The most recent result for Watson was positive, and we are planning to resample. We did run the project through the HORIZON model, and things are looking very promising. The output it gives at the moment is not very friendly to send or view. Its basically a lot of numbers, it requires a lot of interpretation and it is still a prototype, so we aren't going to share the results until we have calibrated it a bit more. It has suggested though that it is very likely that you have had an increase significant enough to be credited a second time around. From next week you will be able to see some of the HORIZON information in the platform - it will show you zones of your best performing, average, and lower performing areas in terms of carbon sequestration. engagements.subject: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Mark and Amanda, Thanks again for your time earlier today and I appreciate you both reconnecting with us here at AgriProve. I've attached the initial project area that the operations team had put together so just wanted to add some context here from prior discussions with Bill Hyem. I believe it would be fair to say based on the prior discussions that you would like to concentrate on the Eidsvold block and the Northern Lot of about 1200Ha which is represented in the mapping attached, is that correct? If anything has changed, please let me know. We would also need to have finish some key parts of the Land Management Strategy Call and Five Year Farm Management History. This accompanies all AgriProve projects and details how your projects are managed and monitored by AgriProve, while ensuring our landholders maintain full management autonomy. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. Below is link to the questions I would cover in a 45 minute call which I work be happy to work toward you calendar and arrange the time to finalize this step. AgriProve Project Proposal: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0msZ20 And below is a link to the Five Year Farm Management History that you would need to only compete the relevant pages on that is directly aligned with you farming enterprise. AgriProve Project Proposal - Farm Management.pdf: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0msS_0 After speaking with Mark this morning is northern property is under irrigation and wasn't effectively utilized in the baseline period by the previous owners as Mark has only just taken over. Lastly, I have provided the link to the eligible practices the you can choose a maximum of 1-2 to implement as part of the project. We will cover this on our Land Management Strategy Call but it will give you a chance to align with what practice would be best applied to your operation. AgriProve Eligible Activities: https://help.agriprove.io/what-do-i-need-to-do-to-build-soil-carbon From Bill's initial notes - Eligible activities included: Altered stocking rate - Increasing fencing infrastructure and water points to improve rotational system for better soil and plant health and performance. Pasture renovations - improve Buffel grass monoculture by increasing species diversity through seeding We would also advise to keep "altering the stocking rate" but we can discuss with you through this process and realign the most applicable practice to your operation. I'll give you a call mid-early next week to discuss further. engagements.subject: RE: Re: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Mark and Amanda, Following on from our visit and checking in with the severe weather that is occurring in your region. Have you had any further questions regarding project design, mapping or registration intent following on from our conversation a fortnight ago? From my notes, the topics we discussed were: Core Concern: Project Design & Configuration Your primary concern was whether work done in certain areas (specifically high country) would materially increase the baseline or disadvantage them. We have addressed this by configuring the project by isolating the high country into a specific project, demonstrating the design was built with their best interests in mind while maximising usability. We will work with you to register projects as you want – we can align this to implementation, baselining or ability for success. It may be that we register the two highest potential projects in the near term, and then look to work out how best to maximise the leucaena country that is more advanced in the carbon and farm improvement approach. Key Context You want to set this project up in line with family succession planning, with your overriding priority is setting it up for long-term success and maximising carbon credit (ACCU) potential. Project Proponent Discussion Your lawyers had advised you to act as project proponent to maintain control of ACCUs. We will set up an ANREU account that your entitlement of ACCUs produced will be transferred to you within 10-business days of being issued, you will have full control for your share of ACCUs. As we discussed, I clarified the additional regulatory and compliance responsibilities that come with that role, and why having those obligations managed externally gives the project the best chance of compliance and success. Implementation / Grazing Management You intend to make grazing management changes but are not interested in intensive cell grazing — you want a more holistic, flexible approach. you want someone on-site to assess what changes are realistic and where the opportunities lie. We can provide you with a video call with our Grazier in Residence (Hobbs Magaret); he will happily provide you with some tangible practice changes that can align to your overall philosophy. We will not likely be able to have Hobbs come to farm, as he is based in Albury. Baseline & Costs Baseline sampling costs were discussed. The upfront cost is not insignificant, but the framing was that carbon income is supplementary — cream on top of the farming enterprise. As mentioned, the baseline costs will be as quoted in the KCT that you have received and is inclusive of all projects, we invoice this on a project by project basis, so there may be a phased costing approach for the baseline sampling, depending on when this occurs. We are also flexible if you choose to split some between upfront payment and future ACCUs (if in the event no ACCUs are generated, this amount is payable at 5-years as per the $ amount (not the ACCU number multiplied by spot price); or on project termination prior to projects being awarded ACCUs.). @Mark – please send through the list of questions that you had, that you raised in the meeting. I will endeavour to respond to these questions as quickly as possible. Regards, Will Frecheville | Head of Operations Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: +61 402 726 315 Email: will@agriprove.io Address: Sunshine Coast, QLD | Head Office: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. If you have any questions related compliance or data protection, please contact our Data Protection Officer . (Satellite mapping? What else?) 5.Will *AgriProve conduct an on-site assessment* to gather information before further estimating potential ACCUs? 6.What is the *estimated carbon income* and *how it is calculated*? 7.What are the *financial risks (for us)* if theproject underperforms or something goes wrong? 8.How will *physical risks* be managed (e.g., fire, flood) and who will bear the cost of any necessary action? *Project Proponent * 10.If AgriProve is the Project Proponent, what legal protections are in place to protect our rights and obligations? 11.AgriProve is shown to be the Project Proponent: a) are they willing to allow us (Mark and Amanda) to be the Project Proponents? b) If yes to the question above, could AgriProve still do the*sampling and assist with the reporting and other paperwork*? 12.If *AgriProve is wound up* unexpectedly in the future, what happens to our ACCUs? ·Revocation? ·Return of ACCUs? ·Are the ACCU’s assets of the company, to be dealt with by the liquidators? ·Can you identify *where in contracts the protection for us* is on this point? *Services * 13.Please provide further details of the baseline sampling and what is included in the upfront/agreed ACCUs amount (*shown as $16,800 plus GST* or *1344 ACCUs*) 14.What are the likely *additional products and services* that I may need and what is the estimated Additional Products and Services *Fee* for those services? engagements.subject: Trophy CP (CRD207716) [SEC=OFFICIAL]
engagements.body: OFFICIAL Regarding the Trophy CP (CRD207716), we have identified a few matters in the crediting application. 1. The LMS states that the project proposes to undertake three activities: application of nutrients, re‑establishment of pasture, and alteration of the stocking rate. It is unclear what activities have been undertaken during the reporting period. The Executive Summary indicates that only re‑establishment of pasture and alteration of the stocking rate were completed, however the summary in the Offsets Report states that all three proposed activities have been undertaken. Could you please confirm which version is correct, noting that there is minimal information in the Executive Summary regarding the application of nutrients in the project area? If only two of the three activities have been implemented to date, could you clarify whether the landholder intends to implement all three activities over the project period, or only the two described in the Executive Summary? Please provide this information by the 10th of February 2026. 1. The calculation of project emissions has a few errors: * Livestock emissions: The Offsets Report states that historical stocking rate data was available for the entire baseline period. However, there are entries in equation 16 which suggests that historical records were not available for maiden ewes (eq. 16 also includes entries for other ewes for which historical records were available, perhaps these entries are supposed to be for breeding ewes?). Emissions from maiden ewes (output of equation 15) were not included in the livestock emission calculations (equation 12), and it is unclear whether maiden ewes (and breeding ewes) were present during the baseline period. It is noted that maiden and breeding ewes were present during the reporting period. * Synthetic fertiliser emissions: The incorrect emissions factor in equation 19 was applied for both the baseline and reporting periods. The Queensland value for cotton was used (2.59) instead of the Victoria value for non‑irrigated pasture (1.72). * Baseline and reporting periods: Livestock emissions appear to have been reported over six years rather than five years over both periods; in particular, 365 days were applied to each year during the baseline period. We note that the issue of incorrect baseline periods has previously been raised in regards to other Agriprove projects. As correction of the above errors still result in a negative change in project emissions, an amended offset report is not required to be submitted for this crediting application. However, please address the above matters in the next crediting application. It would also speed up the assessment process for all Agriprove projects if it could be ensured that Offsets Reports for all projects are accurate and consistent with the method. Hi Ken, Great chatting with you just now. I've attached our LMS (Land Management Strategy) for grazing. Also, our CTR/CTI (Consent to Register/Commitment to Implement) which as I mentioned on the phone allows AgriProve to register your property for a soil carbon project/s. It requires signatures from all signatories on the land titles. It is not a requirement that the process carries on past this stage. I have attached the Licence and Sale agreement. This agreement sets out our 25% success fee for all ACCUs generated by the project. Your 75% share of ACCUs generated can be sold as per Schedule 1 of the agreement, and it is up to you as to the relative percentage of Options 1 through 3 that the client would like to select (for example, you could elect to sell 33% at our long-term fixed price, 33% at the spot market price at the time of issuance, and hold 33% for future sale at a time of your choosing). Note also that if you opt in to the advance payment option, Schedule 3 of the agreement will be updated to reflect the ACCUs required to repay the advance payment as outlined above. -The agreement also grants AgriProve the licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit the carbon project/projects for the term of the licence. The key responsibility for you is to maintain the property in an agricultural system. This allows us to complete all the monitoring and reporting requirements of the project, and to manage the administrative requirements in the event that the property or portions of the property are sold in the future. This has been designed to reduce your risks regarding property sales and succession planning. Also note that as a signatory to the Carbon Industry Code of Conduct, we are required to recommend that you seek independent legal and/or financial advice before signing our Sales and Licence Agreement. Regards Michael

engagements.body: Hi Ken, ACCUs are being generated all over Australia — here are some real-world results showing how soil carbon projects are delivering value for producers just in the last few weeks Watson Carbon Project – NSW: https://agriprove.io/watson-carbon-project Geoff Fox and Mitch Lee have achieved a significant milestone by receiving 5,585 ACCUs for their project near Armidale through adaptive grazing and improved groundcover. Not only did they generate ACCU's but they had significant increase in carrying capacity. Fife Carbon Project – VIC: https://agriprove.io/fife-carbon-project This project marks a significant milestone being the first broadacre cropping operation to receive ACCUs for soil carbon sequestration. engagements.subject: Riverina soils might be worth more than you think
engagements.body: G'Day Ken, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as a proud Albury-based business in the region, I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the Riverina region. Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural "carbon sink" where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years. Why This Matters for Carbon: The combination of your soil types, pH management and yearly rainfall combination generate a significant carbon opportunity If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? engagements.subject: How a Riverina farmer is are forecasting success in carbon farming
engagements.body: Ken, Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). I couldn't miss the opportunity to tell you about another Riverina farmer doing something pretty remarkable. engagements.subject: What is Soil Carbon and Why is it Important for Your Farm?
engagements.body: Hi John​, I wanted to reach out to fill you in with some helpful resources on soil carbon and why it's important for any farming operation. Soil carbon refers to the organic carbon stored within the soil, derived from plant and animal residues that have undergone decomposition. It plays a pivotal role in soil health and fertility. It enhances soil structure, water retention, and nutrient availability, thereby improving crop productivity and resilience to environmental stresses such as drought and extreme weather events. Increased soil carbon helps the overall health of your farm leading to increased long-term sustainability, productivity and profitability. Here is a link to a short explainer video: "How to Grow Top Soils": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xj5uS_cB8nA&t=1s Are you interested in exploring how you can generate revenue from your soil? engagements.body: Hi John​, Just following up on my previous email, I wanted to highlight ways our partnering farmers have generated income from their soils. engagements.subject: RE: Killen CP - Farm Records
engagements.body: Hi John, To further clarify the below: Methodology Reference Amount Change Comment Change in soil organic carbon stock in the CEA with a specified probability of exceedance for a reporting period (Eqn69) 975.2 tC Inclusive of the first reporting period discount of 25% on estimated stocks. Change in soil organic carbon stock in the project are for the reporting period (Eq6) (Refer to below) 563.2 tC / 2065.8 tCO2e - 412 tC / 1,510.667 tCO2e -412 tC is the Q_NSF,CEA, as the total tonnes of Carbon added to the CEA in the form of non-synthetic fertiliser during the reporting period. In this case, it is the amount of carbon in the drinking water sludge, as specified in the farm records) Emissions due to performing the eligible activities on the project area 82.84 tCO2e (Net increase of 41.42 tCO2e vs baseline per year) Inclusive of the livestock increases, and emissions due to the AgriAsh and Drinking Water Sludge being considered ‘Lime’ Estimated Net Abatement 1982.96 (2065.8 tCO2e – 82.84 tCO2e); -82.84 TCO2e Change in SOC_RP.PA (Eqn 6) – Emissions_RP.PA – converted into tCO2e ACCU Estimation 1487 -25% -495.96 tCO2e Net Abatement(NAN), less CER Risk of Reversal Discount (5%) and Permanence Period Discount (20%). Calculated as NAN – (NAN*RoR[5%])-(NAN*Perm.Period[20%]) Rounded down to the nearest whole number. Landholder Entitlement 1116 -25%, -371 tCO2e Estimated ACCUs after AgriProve is paid our 25% success fee. With any partial ACCU being distributed to the landholder, to ensure AgriProve’s success fee is never more than 25%. Equation 6 [cid:image010.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] Where: [cid:image011.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] [cid:image012.png@01DAACF0.645547D0] This means that in order to determine the amount of change in carbon stock in the project area for the reporting period, we need to deduct any non-synthetic fertiliser that contains carbon from the change in carbon measured and reported to you prior to gathering farm records. In this instance, the organic carbon content (as supplied, and by using the Walkley-Black Method, it is safe to assume that is organic carbon) is 12.5% per L applied, and the quantity applied is equivalent to 168 tC and 244 tC is as detailed in the farm records. We must, as specified by the method, deduct this addition from the measured change in soil carbon stocks. It is also worth noting, that if we did not, that both the auditors and CER would identify this, and we would be required to deduct this amount at their insistence. It is important to note a couple of things here: 1. This is the first offsets report, at year 2 in a 25-year project. It has the 25% first reporting discount applied to the carbon stock, prior to any other discounts – this will be removed in the next reporting period. 2. If, the carbon levels are maintained, and the drinking sludge is not applied during a reporting period, and a claim is made for ACCUs, then the tonnes of carbon in the sludge will not be deducted from the change in carbon stock as it has been for this round. 3. For a 48Ha project, an increase and project ACCU claim (estimated) of 1487 ACCUs, is an astoundingly good result, and is the equivalent of 15.5 ACCUs/Ha/Yr. As an estimation of ‘sequestration’ this is 4.22 tC/Ha/yr. 4. This result may change depending on the auditors/CER determination, and is not final. Please call me if you wish to discuss. engagements.subject: Killen CP - Site Audit Visit - Tuesday 18th June
engagements.body: Hi John, In preparation for the Site Visit on Tuesday 18th June, I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. Please see the attached agenda for the site visit, and a couple of aspects that will be discussed as well as the following questions. 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of FMR dates) 2. Detailed description of all land management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points. Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically farm house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the farm, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to farm house/office - interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that farm records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the farm records (such as livestock, invoices for inputs (AgriAsh, DWT Sludge), contracts or invoices or records of spreading/incorporations of activities * Confirmation that we (yourself and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the Carbon project operation, implementation and administration I am happy to set up a meeting with you later next week to discuss this in further detail. Please let me know if you have any availability. engagements.subject: RE: Killen CP - Farm Records
engagements.body: Hi Will, Can you please clarify from the table below, that if we hold the carbon we added (421tC) at the T2 measurement, we’ll get the 1,510.667 tCO2e back? That is, the 421 tonnes doesn’t get added to the T0 baseline. Regards, John John Lawson MEngSc (UNSW) Dip Tech Civ Eng (NSWIT/UTS) Director SoilRegen Pty Ltd 376 Blakney Creek Road North, BLAKNEY CREEK NSW 2581 Mobile: 0438 873 475 Ph: +61 438 873 475, ABN: 38 168 154 327 Web: www.soilregen.com.au [cid:image001.jpg@01DB163B.91F9F280] We recycle industrial byproducts to improve soil structure and biology for better crops and stock From: Will Frecheville Sent: Thursday, 23 May 2024 10:07 AM To: John Lawson Subject: RE: Killen CP - Farm Records Hi John, To further clarify the below: Methodology Reference Amount Change Comment Change in soil organic carbon stock in the CEA with a specified probability of exceedance for a reporting period (Eqn69) 975.2 tC Inclusive of the first reporting period discount of 25% on estimated stocks. Change in soil organic carbon stock in the project are for the reporting period (Eq6) (Refer to below) 563.2 tC / 2065.8 tCO2e - 412 tC / 1,510.667 tCO2e -412 tC is the Q_NSF,CEA, as the total tonnes of Carbon added to the CEA in the form of non-synthetic fertiliser during the reporting period. In this case, it is the amount of carbon in the drinking water sludge, as specified in the farm records) Emissions due to performing the eligible activities on the project area 82.84 tCO2e (Net increase of 41.42 tCO2e vs baseline per year) Inclusive of the livestock increases, and emissions due to the AgriAsh and Drinking Water Sludge being considered ‘Lime’ Estimated Net Abatement 1982.96 (2065.8 tCO2e – 82.84 tCO2e); -82.84 TCO2e Change in SOC_RP.PA (Eqn 6) – Emissions_RP.PA – converted into tCO2e ACCU Estimation 1487 -25% -495.96 tCO2e Net Abatement(NAN), less CER Risk of Reversal Discount (5%) and Permanence Period Discount (20%). Calculated as NAN – (NAN*RoR[5%])-(NAN*Perm.Period[20%]) Rounded down to the nearest whole number. Landholder Entitlement 1116 -25%, -371 tCO2e Estimated ACCUs after AgriProve is paid our 25% success fee. With any partial ACCU being distributed to the landholder, to ensure AgriProve’s success fee is never more than 25%. Equation 6 [cid:image002.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] Where: [cid:image003.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] [cid:image004.png@01DB163B.91F9F280] This means that in order to determine the amount of change in carbon stock in the project area for the reporting period, we need to deduct any non-synthetic fertiliser that contains carbon from the change in carbon measured and reported to you prior to gathering farm records. In this instance, the organic carbon content (as supplied, and by using the Walkley-Black Method, it is safe to assume that is organic carbon) is 12.5% per L applied, and the quantity applied is equivalent to 168 tC and 244 tC is as detailed in the farm records. We must, as specified by the method, deduct this addition from the measured change in soil carbon stocks. It is also worth noting, that if we did not, that both the auditors and CER would identify this, and we would be required to deduct this amount at their insistence. It is important to note a couple of things here: 1. This is the first offsets report, at year 2 in a 25-year project. It has the 25% first reporting discount applied to the carbon stock, prior to any other discounts – this will be removed in the next reporting period. 2. If, the carbon levels are maintained, and the drinking sludge is not applied during a reporting period, and a claim is made for ACCUs, then the tonnes of carbon in the sludge will not be deducted from the change in carbon stock as it has been for this round. 3. For a 48Ha project, an increase and project ACCU claim (estimated) of 1487 ACCUs, is an astoundingly good result, and is the equivalent of 15.5 ACCUs/Ha/Yr. As an estimation of ‘sequestration’ this is 4.22 tC/Ha/yr. 4. This result may change depending on the auditors/CE…

engagements.subject: National Carbon Farming Conference - Albury, 3–6 Nov
engagements.body: Hi Mitch, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out.
