WH William Hyem 19 Jun, 23 Hi Geoff, Please see the attached results for Cooper and Beale soil carbon projects. When the results were returned in June, we did find that some of the samples did not reach the full 30cm depth requirement for the methodology, and so we are likely going to need to resample and potentially re-stratify based on what is known of the area. Also, please find in three separate follow up emails the forwarded Sales and Licence Agreements for all projects, originally sent to gbfox@nidebra.com in December 2021. We have updated our Sales and Licence Agreement since then, so if you have received legal advice on the attached and are happy to sign that’s great – if you have not yet received legal advice please let me know and I will get you a single SLA on the updated terms. The terms are mostly the same, there have been some additions for data management and also non-performance clauses to remove AgriProve as project proponent under certain conditions as well which gives a bit more flexibility. I have attached the terms of the new agreement for your reference. Finally, with regards to invoicing the baseline sampling quote in an email 14/12/2021 was Beale: $4,000 ex. GST upfront and Cooper: $6,000 ex. GST upfront, or $12.50 ACCU forward abatement loan (let me know if you want to discuss this option, I believe last we spoke payment upfront was your preference). There was also the extra cost for agricultural analytes which were sent to yourself and Mitch last year. We have discussed the invoice for Watson Carbon Project previously and we cannot find record in xero or transaction history that this has been paid (original invoice attached). If you have paid this, would you please be able to send through remittance of the transaction? Thank you for your patience, sorry I know we have a bit to work through here but give me a call to discuss as ever on 0456 312 603. Kate MS Mat Silver 18 May, 22 Email sent regarding project support - see Cooper CP notes for a copy. KC Kate Carmichael 30 Sep, 21 RFI on CTR-CTI, needs one more director signature

engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.body: Thanks Jon, Yes – there is an individual identifier for each point, and the results will be aligned to those points. We are required to take 4 sample points within each of the 4-strata areas that make up a project boundary. We have stratified (4x strata) based on soil type, slope, and a range of other factors based on our HORIZON model. Reserve points, are additional points within each strata that we will take, if a primary target point cannot be obtained. We did have to use some reserve points on the property to complete the sampling. engagements.subject: Lead Indicator Assessment positive.
engagements.body: Hi Ella, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is likely worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. I would like to discuss project activities before we mobilise the sampling team. When we speak I would also like to confirm that you are happy for us to come and resample your project areas in April? Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. engagements.subject: RE: AgriProve - Quick Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Ella, Yes, the last 5 years are a bit of blur for me too. Regarding the cost of sampling, AgriProve fully covers the cost of all resampling for the life of the project. We follow a fee for success business model which means we only get paid when you do, in the form of a 25% success fee on ACCU issuances. The Soil Carbon Methodology states that a project must have two sampling events within it's first reporting period (5 years). If we are unable to resample before November it may bring the project into question with the regulator. We have not had to test them on this as very few projects are over 5 years old, but there is a chance they would seek to revoke the project. Our position is flexible with what you would like to do with any credits issued, for example if you would rather hold on to them vs. selling on a spot market. However, we would seek compensation for the agreed amount as quoted in the signed commercial terms agreement when the project started. As per the terms, AgriProve would recover the first 750 ACCUs awarded in the event of successful crediting of the project. From our perspective, and regulatory compliance aside, resampling would be worthwhile given the length of time that has past and continued implementation on your part. It would be good to see how the soils may have improved. Can I request that we have a short discussion on what has been done in terms of management change? We would need to link any carbon sequestration to the change in management. Feel free to give me a call on 0401 101 748 at a time that suits. This is in contrast to your email. I understand you were not involved at the start of this project, but we would appreciate your clarification of where in the contract the advanced payment is mentioned. Thank you for your time Regards Ella

The establishment of this role is part of an increased focus on project implementation support to all our clients. I am getting in touch with you to outline just a few of the practical things we are doing to increase support for you and your soil carbon project. 1. An annual review cycle We are moving to an annual project review cycle that will involve us assessing indicators of soil carbon change and determining whether soil sampling is likely to demonstrate an increase in your carbon stocks. As you are hopefully aware, once baselined all soil monitoring and sampling costs are now covered by AgriProve. Your AgriProve Project Manager will be in contact with you to discuss where your project is at in its annual cycle and if necessary to arrange soil sampling. 2. Technical webinar series with Q&A There is so much going on in agriculture at the moment and much of it relates to practices that can increase soil carbon and farm productivity. We are putting together a list of topics that we will engage speakers to provide a webinar followed by a session to answer all your questions on the topic. Some speakers will be technical specialists and academics, others will be fellow land managers sharing their experience with a particular practice. If you have any topics you would like to see added to this webinar series please email me at mat@agriprove.io 3. Support is just a call away If you have any questions about your soil carbon project please do not hesitate to contact your Project Manager. Your AgriProve Project Manager is: Kate Carmichael 0456 312 603 kate.carmichael@agriprove.io Please also feel free to contact me at any time to discuss any issues you have with your project or feedback you wish to provide on AgriProve service. My contact details are: Mat Silver - Farmer Liaison Manager 0466 302 850 mat@agriprove.io Regards, Mat

engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Christophe, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? See my link below. engagements.subject: Re: Carbon Project - Important Actions
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Christophe, I have chased up your results and attached them to this email. Sorry that there was such a delay on getting them to you. For future, something to be aware of is all of the results automatically go into our online platform where you can see them in there as soon as they are ready. I have checked and you do have an account already set up. As you will see, there has not been a measured increase in soil carbon in this sampling round. While this may be disappointing, it is important to remember that soil carbon projects are a long-term investment, with increase in SOC often taking a long time to be achieved. For next steps: * If you would like to discuss your results and how the math's works I can book you in a call with Will who is the guru on that side of things. * We have a grazier in residence who is available to chat with you about grazing practices and what you can do to increase carbon. * I am working through the 5 year reporting side of things for you with the operations team. We can also book in a time to chat with you and your neighbors to go through HORIZON- are you looking to chat to someone about how horizon works and the layers or more of the practical implementation of it ? Let me know what your looking for and I can arrange the best person to talk too. We recently co-hosted the MLA and AgriProve Soil Carbon Field Day at Adam Gunthorpe’s property, where landholders explored the latest in carbon farming. Our sponsorship and participation at the AWiA Conference highlighted our commitment to supporting women in agriculture as they celebrate 30 years of impact. In other exciting news, the release of the Grazing Land Management (GLM) Method has opened up opportunities for landholders to earn reef credits, contributing to environmental stewardship. We are also proud to announce a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed with the University of New England (UNE), which will leverage IoT technologies to revolutionise grazing management. Stay tuned for more updates on these initiatives! engagements.subject: AgriProve - Request to resample Pearce Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Michael, As part of our process, we have completed the annual review of your project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The assessment has shown an increase in NDRE from the baseline to the current period (please see attached), which suggests resampling the project is worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is used as an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration this does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased, and we will not know until the physical sampling has been undertaken. The attached factsheet has information regarding resampling process but if you have any other questions please let me know. It will be great to get additional results to see how your project is progressing. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have been going on the ground of your project, I will attempt to contact you in the coming days on your mobile. On this call I will confirm that you are happy to go ahead with re-sampling your project. Once you have confirmed we are able to come and re-sample, one of our field technicians will make contact to arrange timing and access. engagements.subject: Re: Pearce CP - Project Continuance.
engagements.body: Thanks Will, I am presently in Cambodia so generally not answering phone calls unless I recognise the number, due to roaming charges. I am a bit surprised that the soil carbon levels have decreased, not sure what's happening there. My recollection is that the samples were taken around April 2025, so if they weren't tested until August 2025 that does seem to be a bit of a delay, not sure if a delay in testing can cause decreases in soil carbon due to microbial activity? Re the property, groundcover is generally well maintained and the seasons over the past couple of years have been on the wet side, so I thought with the wet season spelling and the paddock rotations that have been happening, soil carbon should at least be maintained, if not increased. So at this stage I am inclined not to proceed any further with the project, seeing as there has been no increase in measured soil carbon over the past 4.5 to 5 years. I will be back in Australia after 20 February 2026 so if you wanted to discuss this on or after 23 February that would be fine. If you are able to contact me via whatsapp that would be fine also, we just need to take account of the three or four hour time difference (9 am here in Cambodia is midday in Qld, 1 pm in NSW/Vic, your call this morning came through at 6.48 am Siem Reap time) and I need to have access to wifi, which I have most of the time (11.30 am to 7.30 pm Qld time). engagements.subject: Deforestation-free Beef Credential
engagements.body: Good afternoon Michael, Thank you for your request for a Deforestation-Free Beef Credential! We at AgriProve are excited to assist your business in ensuring you are at the front of the line to access premium supply chains. We are proud to work together with innovative producers such as yourself to showcase the exemplary management Aussie farmers are globally renown for! How the process will work from here: You complete the attached invoice payment. AgriProve and Verterra complete a full retrospective geospatial analysis to validate your property as compliant with EU, international, and domestic beef purchaser requirements. We provide you with a 3rd party verified, shareable report and a profile badge in your AgriProve platform. You are then able to share this with any interested buyers, banks, or insurers as proof that you are managing in a sustainable manner. If you would like any more information on the credential please feel free to read about it on the Knowledgebase here: Why is it important to have a Deforestation-Free Beef Credential?: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-the-deforestation-free-beef-credential. Once again - thank you for partnering with AgriProve, we are honoured to assist your enterprise in articulating your management to the market. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions. engagements.subject: Grazing Management Changes and Timeline
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Thanks for your time just before, as discussed, the CER has asked about the grazing practice changes you have made. Specifically, the first water upgrades in 2021, and some sub-divisions of paddocks. We need to show a clear timeline of additional fencing upgrades/changes post the April 2022 declaration, as well as changes to stocking rates/durations of grazing following the seeding and application of Rural Boss. When we were on site, I remember you saying you're constantly making changes, based on behaviours to optimise the approach and your grazing management, so I do not think we will have an issue showing this change. As a first step, whilst you're putting together some timelines against your notes, can you please send me some photos of your grazing charts (as many years back as you have) We did have an option to not have grazing included as an eligible activity, however given it is central to your operation, I do not want to let this eligible activity go. The positive is that whilst there is a query on this aspect of grazing, the other implementation activities of pasture rejuvenation and nutrient application (Rural Boss spray) have been accepted and there is no risk to the overall application of credits. Appreciate your help. Feel free to give me a call to discuss. engagements.subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. Kind regards, Dylan Jones | Soil Carbon Operations Officer Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: +61 401 101 748 Email: djones@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. From: Jeff Bell Sent: Sunday, 2 February 2025 2:55 PM To: Dylan Jones Subject: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Dylan, The Agriprove platform said "Generate income through a Reef Credit project Your property is eligible to undertake a Reef Credit Project." Is this correct or is it just that we are geographically eligible? Can a reef credit project co-exist with a carbon project? I have been looking into "natural sequence farming" which is all about keeping water and dissolved nutrients on farm through modifying existing contour drains and/or constructing level contours.(which fits neatly into what the "reef credit project" would be looking to achieve. Attended a "natural sequence farming" field day yesterday and there was so much that explained why areas of our farm have limited performance compared to the mean. If we spend money on training and earthworks to keep more water and nutrients on our farm(approx 94 % of which is under a carbon project) would we be eligible for a "reef credit project"? Jeff Bell

engagements.subject: Re: Re questions re "Reef Credits"
engagements.body: Hi Dylan, Definitely would not be grazing management as that is already done. It would be remedial earth works to modify the existing drain contours and where needed construct new contours to slow the flow of water and nutrients and keep both on farm rather than running off down the waterway which does come in the list of gully management methodology activities. Most of the farm can benefit from this in productivity(and consequently carbon sequestration) but only about 30 percent of the farm(my guestimate) has substandard ground cover which in my opinion could release some sediment and nutrients off farm. My take is that the amount of sediment lost from the farm in its current condition would be to low to bother with. The only place where there would be any amount would be a bit hard to manage as it comes pouring through from next door in a water way only a couple of hundred metres from our bottom fence. If Agriprove think there is anything worth pursuing then I will think about it. I myself think not but that is an opinion not based on knowledge. From: Dylan Jones Sent: Monday, 3 February 2025 10:11 AM To: Jeff Bell Cc: Bill Hyem Subject: RE: Re questions re "Reef Credits" Hi Jeff, Yes, the platform is basing its assessment of eligibility off geographical location within the reef catchment areas. A Reef Credit project and Soil Carbon sequestration project can co-exist and we are actively targeting those landholders with an existing project with us that may be interested in Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management (GLM) method. I’ll pass your query over to Bill Hyem in our team to look further into this for you. Natural sequence farming seems like it would be a great addition to the property from my limited knowledge on it, and should help reduce fine sediment loss and nutrient runoff. However, there are some points to be aware of to be eligible for a GLM Reef credit project: * one or more additional or new management activities is implemented, * management activities are reasonably expected to improve ground cover for water quality improvement that are beyond what is required by legislation or pre-existing formal obligations, * grazing is the principle land use for the last seven years, and * broad scale clearing of woody vegetation has not occurred within the previous seven years. From the looks of it, if you were to start a reef credit project based purely on implementing natural sequence farming principles the project would go under the “Gully Method” which involves landscape rehabilitation and construction. We may struggle to prove additionality under the Grazing method as it would need to be a new activity relative to what you’re already doing with the carbon project. See attached guidance on Reef credits under the Grazing Land Management Methodology. We’ll get back to you with our thoughts after reviewing the situation further. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Jeff, I have just completed your yearly satellite assessment for your carbon project. As you know we use this as an indicator for if we think resampling would be worthwhile. Your assessment this year ( attached) has shown an increase in the average NDRE from baseline to current period and an increase in the past year. This indicates that re-sampling this year would be worthwhile. Please note that while NDRE is an indicator there are many other factors that can influence sequestration. This does not guarantee that soil organic carbon has increased. We need to complete the physical sampling to know what is happening in the ground. Next steps: Before we schedule the resampling date, we need to complete the phone call section of the review. Is there a time next week that would suit to do that? I have some prep I need to do before the call so locking in a time in advance works best. If you have any questions please let me know. Talk soon. Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61 498 664 218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:3d7261ff-c891-4849-ad36-645ab0eda247] [cid:f301fe00-ff21-4b73-9fa2-956a828f9cce] [cid:f2663d93-f230-4c07-be33-d7023d883512] [cid:1be732a4-a6cf-4d4f-9f87-11c9d3beebb2] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Follow up from Friday's conversation
engagements.body: Hi Mark, Thanks again for the chat last Friday. I just wanted to response to you based off your questions regarding AgriProve remains at the forefront of Australia’s soil carbon industry, having delivered the country’s first soil carbon credits, pioneered digital MRV systems and registered over 600 projects nationwide with more than 120,000 Australian Carbon Credit Units issued to date. We have invested 25 million dollars into satellite monitoring and carbon forecasting algorithms to addressable Australian Carbon market. AgriProve was named AFR Sustainability Leaders Winner in Agriculture and Environment Recognising Innovative Technology last year. that Delivers Rapid Results and have recently received an $11.5 million dollar grant. AgriProve has successfully completed the $11.55 million National Soil Carbon Innovation Challenge (NSCIC) grant, finalising development of its groundbreaking Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) model in partnership with EOS Data Analytics. Built using over 20,000 physical soil samples and more than 300 predictors, the model combines multi-band SAR and optical data through a Random Forest ensemble machine learning approach to accurately estimate SOC stocks across Australia’s diverse landscapes. Once your project is registered, you will have access to the SOC model in the next 2-3 months to calibrate the monthly level which will effectively analyze your carbon stocks. The company continues to work closely with industry, government and scientific partners to expand participation and strengthen Australia’s position as a global leader in carbon removal through agriculture, so we plan on being here for a very long time. As far as the 25 year longevity of the project, AgriProve will conduct a 5 year project review to access the viability of the project. This is a anniversary review of the declaration of your project and the opportunity to review performance. If no increases have occurred you have the right to delist the project with no obligations or costs to you as the landholder. engagements.subject: RE: Re: AgriProve Soil Carbon Project Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Mark and Amanda, Following on from our visit and checking in with the severe weather that is occurring in your region. Have you had any further questions regarding project design, mapping or registration intent following on from our conversation a fortnight ago? From my notes, the topics we discussed were: Core Concern: Project Design & Configuration Your primary concern was whether work done in certain areas (specifically high country) would materially increase the baseline or disadvantage them. We have addressed this by configuring the project by isolating the high country into a specific project, demonstrating the design was built with their best interests in mind while maximising usability. We will work with you to register projects as you want – we can align this to implementation, baselining or ability for success. It may be that we register the two highest potential projects in the near term, and then look to work out how best to maximise the leucaena country that is more advanced in the carbon and farm improvement approach. Key Context You want to set this project up in line with family succession planning, with your overriding priority is setting it up for long-term success and maximising carbon credit (ACCU) potential. Project Proponent Discussion Your lawyers had advised you to act as project proponent to maintain control of ACCUs. We will set up an ANREU account that your entitlement of ACCUs produced will be transferred to you within 10-business days of being issued, you will have full control for your share of ACCUs. As we discussed, I clarified the additional regulatory and compliance responsibilities that come with that role, and why having those obligations managed externally gives the project the best chance of compliance and success. Implementation / Grazing Management You intend to make grazing management changes but are not interested in intensive cell grazing — you want a more holistic, flexible approach. you want someone on-site to assess what changes are realistic and where the opportunities lie. We can provide you with a video call with our Grazier in Residence (Hobbs Magaret); he will happily provide you with some tangible practice changes that can align to your overall philosophy. We will not likely be able to have Hobbs come to farm, as he is based in Albury. Baseline & Costs Baseline sampling costs were discussed. The upfront cost is not insignificant, but the framing was that carbon income is supplementary — cream on top of the farming enterprise. As mentioned, the baseline costs will be as quoted in the KCT that you have received and is inclusive of all projects, we invoice this on a project by project basis, so there may be a phased costing approach for the baseline sampling, depending on when this occurs. We are also flexible if you choose to split some between upfront payment and future ACCUs (if in the event no ACCUs are generated, this amount is payable at 5-years as per the $ amount (not the ACCU number multiplied by spot price); or on project termination prior to projects being awarded ACCUs.). @Mark – please send through the list of questions that you had, that you raised in the meeting. I will endeavour to respond to these questions as quickly as possible. engagements.subject: Carbon Projects Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Geoff and Mitch, I am getting in touch as I have completed the annual satellite review of your carbon projects. These use satellite NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) data to get an idea of if the vegetation in the projects has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample. As you will see in the attached document: The Watson Carbon Project has had a positive indicator suggesting that resampling would be worthwhile. We have also run this through HORIZON and it has backed that up. This means carbon sequestration is likely, and we are intending to resample this project asap. The Cooper & Beale Projects had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it is an indicator that suggests that the positive change has not been more since baseline and therefore carbon sequestration is unlikely to have occurred. These have not met the threshold for resampling at this time. In the next few months when we have our HORIZON model up and running we will be able to do a regular assessment of these with more factors included which will give us more information and trigger a resampling when it is indicated. The next steps are that the operations team will reach out to talk about sampling logistics and we will need to start preparing the Cooper and Beal projects for their audit as they are coming up to 5 year anniversaries at the end of this year. We will be in touch with more information. If you need anything before then feel free to reach out. engagements.body: Hi Dylan, I will look into this in the coming weeks. From our perspective, the first thing we will need to consider is whether we continue with the projects. Should we continue, I will address your other questions and requests. Cheers Paul McDougall Manager - Natural Capital Paraway Pastoral Company Limited 70 McNamara Street | PO Box 22, Orange NSW 2800 M: 0414 344 464 paul.mcdougall@paraway.com.au www.paraway.com.au [cid:image007.jpg@01DB7942.4B0765A0] From: Dylan Jones Sent: Tuesday, 7 January 2025 2:17 PM To: Paul McDougall Subject: [EXT] AgriProve - Steam Plains / Perry's Paddock Carbon Projects Caution: This is an email from an external source. Please take care when clicking on links or opening attachments. Hi Paul, Thanks for speaking with me earlier. Providing an update for you to get you up to speed on the status of the soil carbon projects. Let's pick this up again when you return from leave late Jan. As they stand, no commercial agreement was put in place between Paraway and AgriProve, so we'd want to come to some formal arrangement moving forward. I believe there had been some past discussions around the 25% AgriProve success fee on future ACCUs, and Paraway seeking to retain 100% of ACCU issuances. We are happy to come to an agreement there, the only consideration would be that the projects have entered their 5th year of existence and would therefore be due to be externally audited at the end of their first reporting period (5 years). We would ask that a commercial agreement that establishes AgriProve has the legal right to operate the projects on the landholder's behalf be in place prior to August 2025. The carbon projects were declared conditionally by the Clean Energy Regulator, meaning the consent of each relevant interest-holder to the existence of the project must be obtained before the end of the first reporting period. In this case, we would seek the signatures of two current directors of the following entities: Registered Proprietor: Macquarie Agricultural Funds Management No.2 Pty Limited (ACN: 611 566 217) Mortgagee: National Australia Bank Leasee: Paraway Pastoral Company Ltd AgriProve will work through the process of obtaining these signatures in due course with your assistance if required. Both the Perry's Paddock and Steam Plains Carbon Projects exhibit positive trends in their satellite-derived NDRE data indicators since the projects were baselined in 2020. This suggests it would be worthwhile resampling the projects to obtain another round of soil data to compare their respective carbon stocks. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project's registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. Cheers Paul [cid:image007.png@01DC1BF2.B72AE6F0] Paul McDougall Manager - Natural Capital Paraway Pastoral Company Limited 70 McNamara Street PO Box 22, Orange NSW 2800 M. 0414 344 464 E. paul.mcdougall@paraway.com.au www.paraway.com.au From: Dylan Jones Sent: Tuesday, 7 January 2025 2:17 PM To: Paul McDougall Subject: [EXT] AgriProve - Steam Plains / Perry's Paddock Carbon Projects Caution: This is an email from an external source. Please take care when clicking on links or opening attachments. Hi Paul, Thanks for speaking with me earlier. Providing an update for you to get you up to speed on the status of the soil carbon projects. Let's pick this up again when you return from leave late Jan. As they stand, no commercial agreement was put in place between Paraway and AgriProve, so we'd want to come to some formal arrangement moving forward. I believe there had been some past discussions around the 25% AgriProve success fee on future ACCUs, and Paraway seeking to retain 100% of ACCU issuances. We are happy to come to an agreement there, the only consideration would be that the projects have entered their 5th year of existence and would therefore be due to be externally audited at the end of their first reporting period (5 years). We would ask that a commercial agreement that establishes AgriProve has the legal right to operate the projects on the landholder's behalf be in place prior to August 2025. The carbon projects were declared conditionally by the Clean Energy Regulator, meaning the consent of each relevant interest-holder to the existence of the project must be obtained before the end of the first reporting period. In this case, we would seek the signatures of two current directors of the following entities: Registered Proprietor: Macquarie Agricultural Funds Management No.2 Pty Limited (ACN: 611 566 217) Mortgagee: National Australia Bank Leasee: Paraway Pastoral Company Ltd AgriProve will work through the process of obtaining these signatures in due course with your assistance if required. Both the Perry's Paddock and Steam Plains Carbon Projects exhibit positive trends in their satellite-derived NDRE data indicators since the projects were baselined in 2020. This suggests it would be worthwhile resampling the projects to obtain another round of soil data to compare their respective carbon stocks. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project's registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. Please take care when clicking on links or opening attachments. Hi Paul, Thanks for speaking with me earlier. Providing an update for you to get you up to speed on the status of the soil carbon projects. Let's pick this up again when you return from leave late Jan. As they stand, no commercial agreement was put in place between Paraway and AgriProve, so we'd want to come to some formal arrangement moving forward. I believe there had been some past discussions around the 25% AgriProve success fee on future ACCUs, and Paraway seeking to retain 100% of ACCU issuances. We are happy to come to an agreement there, the only consideration would be that the projects have entered their 5th year of existence and would therefore be due to be externally audited at the end of their first reporting period (5 years). We would ask that a commercial agreement that establishes AgriProve has the legal right to operate the projects on the landholder's behalf be in place prior to August 2025. The carbon projects were declared conditionally by the Clean Energy Regulator, meaning the consent of each relevant interest-holder to the existence of the project must be obtained before the end of the first reporting period. In this case, we would seek the signatures of two current directors of the following entities: Registered Proprietor: Macquarie Agricultural Funds Management No.2 Pty Limited (ACN: 611 566 217) Mortgagee: National Australia Bank Leasee: Paraway Pastoral Company Ltd AgriProve will work through the process of obtaining these signatures in due course with your assistance if required. Both the Perry's Paddock and Steam Plains Carbon Projects exhibit positive trends in their satellite-derived NDRE data indicators since the projects were baselined in 2020. This suggests it would be worthwhile resampling the projects to obtain another round of soil data to compare their respective carbon stocks. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project's registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. We would ask that a commercial agreement that establishes AgriProve has the legal right to operate the projects on the landholder’s behalf be in place prior to August 2025. However, resampling is conditional on active implementation of the project’s registered eligible activity; re-establishing or rejuvenating pasture. We would therefore like to know the following: * Has the activity been implemented post-baseline? Can you specify which date the implementation activities started. * Has implementation of the activity been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? * Over what proportion of your overall project area has the activity been implemented to date? Look forward to discussing the projects with your further. Last communications from you regarding the above email was that you were needing to determine whether you wished this project to continue. If this is the case, the above items will need to be actions with urgency. We will need to complete the subsequent resampling prior to 15-November-2025. We will need to as a first step have the AgriProve commercial agreement signed, and we can have some discussions on the broader ACCU commercial arrangement. If you do not wish to continue, please let me know and I will action appropriately. I am happy to discuss results and any of the above, please feel free to reach out for any of your questions. engagements.subject: AgriProve Tags for tonnes software - setup session
engagements.body: Hi Justin, Booking some time for us to set you up in the new AgriProve Software. It should take no more than 30 minutes. Let me know if you need us to reschedule. Basic steps that we’ll guide you through are: We’ll email you an invite to the software – you set up a password and login. We’ll get you to set up your own Ceres Portal at https://manage.cerestag.com/account/register - you set up a login and add your property as a location. We’ll guide you in your Ceres portal to claim the tags that we’ll transfer to you We’ll help you to link the AgriProve software And then we can give an overview – or we can let you have a browse and reconvene in a few days. Once were all set we can send invitation to your farm software to any other users who you’d like to have access Speak to you then. discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

engagements.subject: Tags for Tonnes Webinar, 2nd May 12pm AEST
engagements.body: Hi Justin, Great to be connected with you, and thank you for your feedback and time over the phone. Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.subject: Sustainability certification questions
engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs
engagements.body: Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…
