Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.subject: Sustainability certification questions
engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs
engagements.body: Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: AgriProve Tags for tonnes software - setup session
engagements.body: Hi Justin, Booking some time for us to set you up in the new AgriProve Software. It should take no more than 30 minutes. Let me know if you need us to reschedule. Basic steps that we’ll guide you through are: We’ll email you an invite to the software – you set up a password and login. We’ll get you to set up your own Ceres Portal at https://manage.cerestag.com/account/register - you set up a login and add your property as a location. We’ll guide you in your Ceres portal to claim the tags that we’ll transfer to you We’ll help you to link the AgriProve software And then we can give an overview – or we can let you have a browse and reconvene in a few days. Once were all set we can send invitation to your farm software to any other users who you’d like to have access Speak to you then. Cheers TH ________________________________________________________________________________ Microsoft Teams Need help? discovery call with Justin: feedback for becoming a growth engine: We are busy - the life of the carbon project together - need to be able to bring forward the milestones of a carbon project. Key Pieces of Feedback: Transparency Transparency with the operational procedure - "were busy running our own businesses, put together a piece so farmers have an understanding of key times and what is required by the farmer - i.e. a piece of collateral that reflects the project lifecycle" Project Milestones Contact points Regular touch points either en masse or 1:1 AgriProve needs to come in to guide the project and where it needs to go. Goal oriented: Validate that carbon sequestration is possible Was "Mr Skeptical" and wanted to road-test it, so others could take these thing on. Big gap between Operations and the Producer We need guide Tech notes that come with it as well - when sharing technical information from other projects - we haven't done this very well. Provide the farmer with simple takeaways: So the producer is able to communicate, or guide people in a process where they can verbalise their soil mission - how many tonnes we are trying to sequester. Education is needed regularly - e.g. webinars, seminars, tutorials. attend 3-4 webinars a year - so they're engaged with what is happening reality on pay-offs, discussing the newest content. Value Propositions for Customer Success and Recruitment Linkage between production and carbon building: improvements to farm, lead to increase in production, the co-benefit is carbon. Tags for tonnes helps with this as the co-benefits: Compared the Customer success challenge with Ruminati program - they provide a very strong user experience around Baselining and understanding where they're at; Integrates for day to day farming with the carbon project What does it mean being in a carbon project? Similar thinking to superannuation; payback period is significantly further down the line, but the need to regularly check in on progress is important Vital piece is providing a producer with a really simple, value proposition for starting know that shade is super important, improving water, shade, pasture utilisation The more we can break down those barriers for customer success, if we can get that right, participants will be happier with the model, the model is a bit fractured as a result of not setting clear agendas/milestones/guidance - what is working and not working when it comes to carbon building and production benefit. "what were not doing enough of, investing in the production model, but not investing enough time into learning how this relates this back to carbon farming." Long term goal: asset growth and a carbon project Short term goal: animal production and outcomes from that Align short-term to long-term goals, but adding value and clear linkage between short term and long term goals. AgriProve needs to become a producer-oriented organisation: What would the farmer tell the consumer? I'm in an accredited carbon project and using data driven insights to improve my farm Stakeholders: Processors, get a green premium when speaking with processors on ESG programs Banks: Potentially beneficial interest rate when engaging with an ESG Program Teys - Grasslands - they pay a premium for productivity JBS - pay a premium for being a steward of their land Processors - they are talking about the ESG program, but not sure what that program looks like: what sort of value they can give people how do we attach benefits to the 240 farmers, will they get a better rate at the bank? What if they got 0.2% better rate because they're joined to an ESG program with AgriProve. Consumers: Reason other tech companies he's worked with have been successful: AgriWebb gives you a stewardship program, but AgriProve does not - need collateral, AgriProve Environmental Farming Program. "Bank is stoked that you're part of a carbon project, they really look at ESG We will get a premium to these 240 participants? Apart from Off-se…

Chat with Justin RE: Ruminati (8th May 24) Ruminati provide tangible accounting of farm management decisions Moving from what we think we know to something visual and easy to interact with What value prop can we give our customers - something like this is perfect for client interaction We need to have an active mechanism to give this sort of information Currently our emissions discussions are not a good visual representation of management decisions (spreadsheet based) Wen need to (through a tool like this) give them (our landholders and prospects) active scenarios with calcs of how their management changes would effect their carbon balance We need to go on a competitor watch and see the partners they are creating (highly influential) - would give us massive market penetration to partner with Ruminati What does this really give a farmer? - speeds up the process to get a quicker result on the validation piece to their management This is what we are lacking in our offering - pathways to get to net a quicker result - how do we make it easier to do a carbon audit Gives our landholders a triple A rating - auditing - great baseline tool that is farmer and supply chain accepted + government validated emissions sequestration AP should do a validation every 6 months - would be significantly easier and less time consuming with a product such as this AgriProve could provide EOFY Ruminati report AP shouldn't want to replicate the same product - partner and make a commercial agreement - and make the exponential progress Look at who they are ready integrated to - leverage their network We are a $150,000 (300 clients at $500 each) client for 25 years - that's a huge value add for them Want to have tools in the tool box - already have ceres tags and the soil testing internally - this could be a great add-on Rumninati cover the negative aspect - emissions - why wouldn't we look to just buy them out? And tell the whole story Bring on their existing clients and tell the other half of the story Gotta tell the positive - they will want to bring that in their suite of products - they don't do the positive aspects but they are tied in to a suite of partners As a farmer with their service you pay just to know you are a polluter - let us tell your positive aspect - fill their gap with landholders they already have on-board Create a licence agreement or partnership or a pathway for integrating into their clientele Potential for a commercial subscription? Once landholders are signed up create a baseline score for them and give them the option to play with management scenarios Works hand in hand with our products Helps grass fed producers get better market access - we need to look at end producer - grassfed programs Justin sees holes in his story - these are hard to explain - this plugs a massive hole - need to work on our enemy (emissions story tellers) Go to end user - Coles - pitch our product to tell whole picture - negative and positive - do you want to know more - show them Ready Graze with carbon accounting Justin wants $0.20 more per every kg produced due to validation - hard to make a profit right now because of the market - needs to show something different More market access for the positive management the more money landholders can put into the management of their carbon project

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Spoke to Justin about the certification and sustainability piece. Gave great responses, very interested

Responses to sustainability questionnaire: Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? - Yes - GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy - If no, then why not? - N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? - GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management - How can we make the testing attractive and simple - Very honourous - Teas - JBS - TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? - Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? - If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business - Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? - Not direct to consumers - Have looked at the big supply chains - Looked into Greenham’s - Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand - Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? - TBD - Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to - Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals

engagements.body: Good afternoon Justin, Thank you for being so generous with your time today. Below are the responses to the questions we discussed. Have you looked into any sort of sustainability certifications for your produce? * Yes * GBSS – quite honorous, farmer would struggle as it is a invasion of privacy If no, then why not? * N/A Are you aware of any sustainable produce certifications that are of interest to you? * GBSS – testing actually assists in the agronomic management * How can we make the testing attractive and simple * Very honourous * Teas * JBS * TFI Would you want be interested in actively participating a sustainability program to achieve certification for your produce? * Yes Would you be willing to pay for a consultant to handle the monitoring and administration to ensure you are compliant to meet accreditation for a sustainability certification? * If there was a pathway – offer the service from hyour business * Help their clients – how can Costello rural help develop something and roll out to their clients Are you currently or have you looked into direct sales, to consumers or to a retailer or other markets where your objective is to command a premium price for your produce? * Not direct to consumers * Have looked at the big supply chains * Looked into Greenham’s * Yes – Provenir – not worth it themselves, need a group as you need to build a brand * Going to Singapore to set up a brand for produce What would you like AgriProve to invest in to help you as a carbon farmer? * TBD * Time that it takes to get the credits and have them issued – takes a long time to commercialise the payment – where are the small wins – AP to offer pathways to access merchandise, or fertilisers, education and brands to market to * Carbon concierge – concierging the whole program – project, stimulants/seed – markets for the animals Kind regards, Dylan

Hi Justin, I hope you are going well! Lovely to chat to you last week about our research project with RMIT University, about our sampling study, the Australian Soil Carbon Sampling Optimisation Study. As discussed, please see attached the sampling plan, for your approval. RMIT would like to sample only CEA 1, the highest performing CEA, and to resample T0, T1, and T2 points to understand change over time. They would also like to sample 2 extra points at each point 1m and 2m out, like the diagram below, to gain and understanding of spatial variability at a high resolution. Also please note in the plan attached, not all labels are showing due to them being too close together. Please note that this will have no impact on your compliant project sampling rounds and this data is not shared with the regulator. However, this sampling may be used to assist us to better stratify your project to reduce variability within strata. Please let me know if you are happy with this plan. We aim to sample next week, and the guys will be in touch direct to arrange a time. We have also sent you a consent form via panda docs, to say that you are happy for AgriProve to share this data with RMIT for the purposes of the study. Thanks again for being part of the project and please feel free to give me a call if you’d like to discuss. Melanie

engagements.subject: Call with Justin Costello
engagements.body: Chatted to JC about his ACCUs and sharing his profile. He has an idea around the data we are collecting and wanting to create a provenance story using combined AP data and genomics. Looking to put together a proposal to articulate his ideas. Notes from meeting below: Need to validate outcomes Outcomes of carbon project aligned with high quality cattle management AgriProvenance - a failsafe system to prove the traceability Genomics - outcomes of the cattle (when the herd is at feed conversion) T4T, EOS, genomics = package to producers Genomically verify all the bulls - create auditable trails Prove the animals are the best ranking in a carbon sense Potentially use Gallagher / optiweigh and validate the measurements Collect the information and overlay into the program - herd/provenance Each animal verified through genomics, lifetime carbon project measured, kgs produced, kgs emitted, ongoing efficiencies - totalling a value MSA graded product vs reliability Whole of life information - green training wheels on the animal Breed outcome - market ready at a certain time Steer select - animals that will produce best on farm AgriProvenance , net emissions, credits, management strategy - making the farm very transparent Metrics - DOB Genomic testing $40 per head - data to make key decisions Give the data to make an assumption after birth (6 months) these are my highest ranking individuals - keep only the efficient animals on farm (carbon benefit based on efficiency) Improvement on feed efficiency and outcomes Making decisions based on long-term gains Is breeders are inefficient they enter the food supply Over the carbon project you have a high performing herd - go to for efficiencies AgriProvenance adds value to customer - health protocol, vaccine's, health status What AP has is soil - JC can provide the stable products Provenance also goes into the grains/timber, etc. Real tool is good outcomes Validation of bloodline, performance, and carbon story - QR to public page (T carbon produced, T carbon emitted, carbon story and ACCUs) Everything auditbale in a CP and passing audits Best practice and best management that is scalable Go and target Angus Australia

engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Mountain View/Page/Truss CPs
engagements.body: Dear Justin, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: Carbon Project- Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Justin, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. Next year we will review your project again to decide if resampling would be worthwhile. Please note: This trend does not mean carbon has gone backwards, it shows the trend in vegetation greenness has been lower than your baseline average and therefore it is unlikely re sampling would be worthwhile at this time. To tick of your requirements for the year, I need to complete a quick check-in call to go over what you have been doing in your project. Is there a time that suits you for me to give you a call in the next few weeks and complete this phone check in? Talk soon. We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Thorby Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi James, As part of our project monitoring process, we have completed the annual review of your Thorby Carbon Project. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used to measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for soil organic carbon sequestration to have occurred on the project. The trend from the baseline to the current period indicates that NDRE has not shown a significant increase to meet our threshold for resampling this year (shown in the attached report). Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I would appreciate if we could go over how things have gone over the last year for you on the property. I’ll attempt to contact you on your mobile in the coming days, but please feel free to reach me on 0408 448 190 at a time that suits you. engagements.body: Called Andrew Smith regarding management on Thorby CP before selling to James Allen in 2023 Management in the project period before sale (2021-2023) Rotational grazing Stopped all synthetics (pesticides, fungicides) - stopped synthetic fert in 2016 Used the following products: Fulvic acid, vermicast liquid, humates, guano, VAM (seed treatment), protozoa brew, pyroag, homemade aneorobic microbe spray used a disc seeder to minimise tillage Retained stubble and grazed sheep Planted whole place to wheat in the last year (all failed and grazed it off)

CS - 6 Monthly Check-in Survey 1. Please Cross-check the eligible activities that were chosen by the landholder at the time of project registration are accurately captured against customer deal in HS: Applying nutrients, Retaining stubble, Converting to reduced or no-till 2. Have your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3-6 months? Notes: Has deep ripped half the property, clay delved (map to be provided) Full stubble retention system Sprayed foliar trace elements ZMC and P, kelp Rested for a long period Repaired a lot of fencing since taking over, new gates to isolate paddocks (completed mid '24). 200 head sheep 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3-6 months? Notes: Single fert and manure spread. Pasture lacks vigor Perhaps some calcium or lime 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% 100% Notes: Tilled on half, stubble retained and sprayed 100% 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} Notes: 14 days at most. 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} Notes: One month on average, some paddocks go back into continuous crop so only grazed once a year. 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} Notes: 40ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? Notes: Diary for stock movements, any sprays logged on the GPS. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? Notes: Water infiltration after deep rip has improved dramatically, biomass in crops improved. Velt grass is looking better after reducing stock numbers. Seeing dung beetles for the first time ever! 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3-6 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? Notes: None, just dry last year. 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? Notes: None, but planning on planting trees along fence lines. 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? Notes: Would like to conduct some more nutrient testing when resampling to check levels. P was very low.

engagements.body: Hi Donald, Wendy and Jody Thank you for meeting with me this week to discuss your soil carbon potential project. Firstly to Donald, regarding coming out to the property prior to soil sampling and any contracts being signed, there will be no problem at all with that. We would want to get a good indication that AgriProve has been chosen as the preferred partner prior to hitting the road to Longreach but we are very open to doing this with your blessing. I would suggest that we go through the land management strategy call - prepare our final set of documents and bring them out to you and the family to run through a farm visit and our Carbon Project Plan's in person. For Jody, there were quite a few questions which is what we want. Most will be covered in the Terms and Conditions which I've attached in this email. To address the remaining questions (again, there will be more to come, no doubt) please see below: Question/Concerns: That AgriProve don't do any initial soil testing/sampling prior to baselining and why we don't come out and understand the make up of there land prior to baselining: AgriProve response: We have invested 25 million dollars into satellite monitoring and carbon forecasting algorithms based on 75% of the addressable Australian Carbon market that allows us to have the confidence to ensure the first time we test is for baselining. This is to reduce the cost on the farmer and ensure that any money invested is directly for the purpose of the soil carbon project. Question/Concerns - AgriProve being proponent to the project. AgriProve response: This is a massive positive - we take on all the regulatory and compliance risk for the 25 years of the project. It assists in succession and in the instance you wished to sell the property. When AgriProve acts as the proponent, we assume responsibility for all regulatory compliance, including any legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance. This shifts the compliance risk away from the landholder, allowing them to focus on farm management without worrying about legal responsibilities tied to the carbon project. Having AgriProve as the proponent reduces the landholder’s risk and administrative burden. We handle all communication with the Clean Energy Regulator (CER) and manage the compliance process with our experienced team. By taking on these responsibilities, AgriProve allows landholders to avoid navigating the complex legal and regulatory landscape themselves. AgriProve offers significant flexibility. Landholders have the option to cease active project implementation at any time while AgriProve continues to manage the project administratively, ensuring compliance is maintained and ACCU relinquishment is avoided. If the landholder were the proponent, they would have to take on these administrative responsibilities for a non-active project. AgriProve will arrange for and pay for all other costs related to its administration of the soil carbon project over the life of the carbon project. Link to proponent on AgriProve website: https://help.agriprove.io/faq-agriprove-as-proponent-what-are-the-benefits Question: Jody wanted more information about how ACCU's process works and the how the issuance works. engagements.body: Hi Donald, Wendy and Jody, I hope you are have a good week. I just wanted to get back to you regarding fee structure that was dicussing at the end of our Land Strategy Management Call. In regards to when payment is due - post signing the KCT (Key Terms and Conditions) we will arrange baselining - 50% of the invoice paid up front (when date is set, prior to baselining) and 50% once the test results are received. The two fee structure definitions are advised below: Option 1: Success Fee Model Best for: Farmers looking to minimize upfront costs and prefer a "pay-on-results" model. Cost Component Description Price Baseline Sampling Fee One-off upfront cost for sampling; the only out-of-pocket expense. Final cost set in SLA. $316,553 Success Fee (ACCU Share) AgriProve takes 25% of all issued ACCUs as payment, covering: all admin, reporting, auditing, lab costs, project design, and sampling. 25% of ACCUs ✅ Who this suits: Farmers who don’t want to pay annual fees or make large investments up front. Those wanting to de-risk participation until credits are generated. Option 2: Annual Fee Model Best for: Farmers seeking to maximise their ACCU ownership and have capacity for annual payments. (Only available to farms with projects over 10,000 ha) Cost Component Description Price Development Fee Covers setup, registration, sampling, baseline, Land Management Strategy, and access to carbon tools. $34/ha Annual Implementation & Maintenance Fee Ongoing monitoring, proprietary tech (e.g., soil model, effective rainfall, grazing software), lab, audits, sampling, reporting. $22.50/ha/year Success Fee (ACCU Share) Small 5% of ACCUs retained by AgriProve (farmer keeps 95%). 5% of ACCUs ✅ Who this suits: Farmers who want to retain the majority (95%) of their ACCUs. Farmers who want greater control over their credits and are confident in long-term carbon generation. Those with existing budget for annual operational costs and who see carbon as a longer-term strategic asset. In addition, I have logged the information gathered at out Land Management Strategy Call last week, so we just require the Five Year Farm Management History document and Paddock Mapping (either a shapefile or kml file) to complete the process in order to get your Carbon project plan to you. engagements.body: Hi Donald, Wendy and Jody I hope everyone is well. I am just updating the carbon projects proposal with our Head of Operations, Will Frencheville, and we are looking at ways we can improve the reporting to streamline our activities and record keeping. I think one of the ways is to get the last two pieces of information across to us that includes your five year grazing history and paddock maps so that we can overlay against the CEAs (Carbon Estimation Areas) and then pre-fill for the farm management records. I mentioned this to Donald earlier on the phone today that we have undertaken this process for other current projects and it just takes that heavy lifting away from you with the aim to deliver the Carbon Project Proposal at some stage this week. With your permission, can we please have your authorisation for Maia grazing to pass on the electronic paddock maps for the following properties, for your carbon carbon project. Summary Latrobe Station and Arlington Park are located in Longreach, Central West Queensland, spanning a combined 45,000 acres. The properties, purchased in 1995 and 2001 respectively, became certified organic in 2003. Originally a sheep and cattle enterprise, the operation transitioned in 2018 to focus solely on grazing Droughtmaster cattle. The family operation is run by Donald, Wendy, and their daughter Jody Brown : Donald Brown (69), has spent his life on the land, completed short RCS courses, and hosted a regenerative grazing workshop with RCS’s David McLean and Alejandro Carrillo (Mexico). Jody Brown , who grew up on Latrobe, has a background in the Northern Pastoral industry and runs her own cattle business. She’s active in knowledge-sharing within the cattle industry, helped produce a regenerative rangeland video series, created content for Landcare, and completed several grazing and regenerative agriculture courses. Wendy Brown , raised on a small hobby farm, has worked in business administration and later became a jillaroo. Since partnering with Donald, she’s been actively involved in the stations and attended a DPI Nutrition Edge grass management workshop. Grazing management has evolved from: Many small mobs grazing for months per paddock, To fewer, larger mobs with durations of 2–3 months, And now shifting towards shorter durations (days to weeks) and more frequent rotations , with an aim for weekly moves (not fixed to a calendar). Pasture monitoring and grazing planning tools include: MaiaGrazing and Cibo Labs for grass budgets and grazing management.

engagements.subject: Comments re Agriprove/Latrobe Carbon Project
engagements.body: Hi Donald, Below is the email we sent to you on Monday the 22/9 outlining the agreement and Matt's concerns, please let me know if you have any questions... Thanks for your note and for reviewing the materials. I’m picking this up on behalf of Ben as he is out in the field. To keep things simple, we’ve a) mapped the documents, b) listed exactly what AgriProve provides for its 25% fee and what the Browns pay, and c) responded to your numbered questions directly. Firstly, to appropriately answer some of these questions, we need to provide you with further context regarding AgriProve’s Carbon Project Management, and our partnership approach with farmers. Document map: Key Commercial Terms: this sets out the details to establish legal right, the associated parties and the authority for AgriProve to act as the project proponent for the entirety of the project lifetime, and the acceptance for the cost of the baseline sampling. This also specifies the commercial terms for how the landholder will commercialise their ACCUs. Master T&C: roles and responsibilities for the 25-year project life. Standard Attachments: (i) restricted and prohibited activities under the 2021 Soil Carbon Method, and (ii) AgriProve HSE/Biosecurity for our personnel and contractors. LMS: LMS and LMS:CPP – this is the Land Management Strategy that accompanies the application to the CER for participation in a Soil Carbon Project. The LMS:CPP details the eligible activities the Browns will undertake and on the land that this will be performed on. Draft Sample Plans preliminary areas, exclusions, and strata. Any refinement will not exceed the baseline cap set in the KCT. What AgriProve provides for 25% share of ACCUs: Risk protection as Project Proponent for the full term: regulatory, compliance and reporting responsibility with the CER sits with us. Note that there are no title encumbrances: the project creates no caveats or other encumbrances on Browns’ land titles. Sampling & auditing at AgriProve’s cost: all post-baseline sampling rounds (minimum 4) and all audits (minimum 3). Monitoring, reporting & admin: full lifecycle program management and regulator engagement. Commercialisation flexibility for the Browns’ 75%: fixed/spot sale, hold, or transfer to the Browns’ ANREU within 5 business days of issuance. Farmer-led management: our LMS is outcomes-based, preserving on-farm flexibility (subject to the Method/Act). Continuity & succession: mechanics to avoid project disruption on farm sale/succession. What the Browns pay: Baseline sampling only. AgriProve’s quote is inclusive of mapping, soil core extraction, and laboratory testing, as quoted in the KCT (hard cap). On-farm practice costs (e.g. fencing/labour) are at the Browns’ discretion and are not charged by AgriProve. This is a services-for-ACCUs structure, not a JV: AgriProve has no governance or control over the farm, no title rights, and bears the proponent and lifecycle cost and risk so the Browns’ cash outlay is limited to baseline. AgriProve offers a standard product to all our clients across our 580+ Carbon Project portfolio. With that context in mind, please see responses to your numbered points. I could not see the Carbon Project Licence and Sales Agreement in the pack – please provide this document. The document pack is designed to be read as stated in the document map above. It is not clear from the documents what Agriprove is providing (in terms of services) to receive 25% of the output of the project (especially since the Browns are being asked to pay $300k for start up costs). Could this be listed clearly? Could you also list clearly what costs you expect the Browns to pay? As laid out above, the Browns under this agreement cover the costs of the baseline sampling round only. This is inclusive of mapping, soil core extraction and laboratory testing. This is the only cost that the Browns will pay to AgriProve for the operation of their carbon project. AgriProve’s costs through the lifetime of the…

engagements.body: Dear Ian, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. Kind regards, Will Frecheville | Head of Operations [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: +61 402 726 315 Email: will@agriprove.io Address: Sunshine Coast, QLD | Head Office: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image004.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image005.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image006.png@01DCC784.350283C0] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. That is why we have taken appropriate measures to ensure that the data you have provided to us is always secure. If you have any questions related compliance or data protection, please contact our Data Protection Officer . engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Morrison CPs
engagements.body: Dear Ian, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. Kind regards, Will Frecheville | Head of Operations [AgriProve] Phone: 1300 GO SOIL (1300 46 7645) Mobile: +61 402 726 315 Email: will@agriprove.io Address: Sunshine Coast, QLD | Head Office: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:image003.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image004.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image005.png@01DCC784.350283C0] [cid:image006.png@01DCC784.350283C0] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: RE: Reissue of lab report - Morrison Carbon Project 1 & 2

engagements.body: T0 compliance issue. Field sampling error - Did not collect the minimum requirement of 3 sample points from Strata 3. A reserve point from Strata 2 was incorrectly sampled (MO2T0R4) for point MO2T008, resulting in 4 samples being collected from Strata 2 and only 2 samples from Strata 3. Have raised the possibility with the CER of using this incorrect point as is and for the T0 round to be deemed acceptable. No expecting a positive outcome, likely to proceed with the T1 round as the new compliant baseline event.

engagements.subject: RE: Kelly Carbon Project - Audit Site Visit
engagements.body: Hi Sam, Thank you I will let Will know to be there at 8.00am. Please see an agenda attached for the site visit, the visit should take 2-3 hours at most and will involve a drive around the project area and a chat about the eligible activities you have done so far. I have prepared the following information for our benefit to ensure a smooth and successful visit. The main aspects that will be discussed are specified below: 1. The date the eligible activities started in the CEA (confirmation of dates provided in your farm management record) 2. Detailed description of all land management activities undertaken during the baseline period in the CEA (as per the farm management record) 3. Confirm that all CEAs have been used as pasture/agricultural system during the reporting period 4. Confirm that woody vegetation was not cleared in the project area 5. Confirm that there was no thinning of vegetation occurring on the land 6. Ground truthing of the project boundaries and sample points. Typically, we follow the rough itinerary when on site: * Meet at Greet at the agreed meeting point (typically farm house or entrance) * Site tour to confirm project boundaries, and sample points * During the site tour, this is when most of the conversation will be about the history of the farm, how you've implemented the carbon building activities and what has been performed on the land to date * Return to farm house/office - informal interview / viewing of evidence, records and additional points for clarification * Close out meeting - discuss any points of clarification Overall the purpose of the audit is to address the following: * Confirmation that farm records provided is accurate to what has occurred on site * Evidence for the farm records (such as livestock, invoices for inputs, contracts or invoices relating to management activities * Confirmation that we (yourself and AgriProve) have an open line of communication for risks, implementation and all aspects that are related to the Carbon project operation, implementation and administration Please feel free to call if you have questions. Kind regards, Imogen Hickey | Crediting Specialist AgriProve Pty Ltd Phone: 1300 46 7645 Mobile: +61 402 509 303 Email: imogen@agriprove.io Address: Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. engagements.subject: Carbon Project - Annual Review Results
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Sam and Ryan, I have just completed the annual satellite review of your carbon project. Each year we complete a review via satellite of your project to see if the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) trend on your farm in the past 12 months is indicative of soil carbon sequestration. We compare the recent trend to those of the 5 years prior to baseline sampling. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend compared to the baseline period. This means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. As it is year 5 we may put your project through our new model to determine if we should resample later, but at this stage we will not be resampling and will reassess next year. As you have been credited before, we don't have to do a formal check in call, however if you would like to chat about your project- feel free to give me a call anytime. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Kelly CP
engagements.body: Dear Sam and Ryan, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please list all operators full names, emails, phone numbers Notes: Dan Burnham - Email: burnham.grazing@outlook.com Phone: 0429851100 Emma-Jane Burnham - Email emj.burnham@gmail.com Phone: 0458432770 Address: 597 and 791 Roy’s Road, Thangool, QLD 4716 Lot and Plan Numbers 37/PM147 AND 38/PM147 Please list all landowners full names, emails, phone numbers Notes: Dan Burnham - Email: burnham.grazing@outlook.com Phone: 0429851100 Emma-Jane Burnham - Email: emj.burnham@gmail.com Phone: 0458432770 Please provide a brief history of your farm The Burnham family purchased Stonehaven in 2004 and Glenroy in 2008 on 2,400 hectares combined. The steep country soon prompted the Burnhams to question their management style and encouraged them towards regenerative grazing. The resulting increase in groundcover from an initially cautious beginning has solidified into a deep belief in regenerative grazing methods. Stonehaven and Glenroy have been certified USDA NOP organic, Biodynamic since 2015 and Grassfed certified through Teys program at its inception. The properties are also becoming Regenerative Certified from 2025. The Burnhams currently have a vegetation project underway (avoided clearing) with Green Collar in the last 5 years of 200 hectares. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: [Please include any current agronomic advice] Dan is a 5th generation glazier, he grew up with beef cattle and has been a part of the beef agricultural industry all his life. Emma-Jane has been a teacher for her working life and also comes from a beef production family. Together, they completed the RCS courses starting with a Grazing clinic, followed by the GFP course, Next Steps and finally completed Executive Link in 2020. Certified Grazing BMP (Best Management Practice) Please provide a summary of your soil carbon project philosophy and goals: Our goal at Burnham Grazing is to have biodiversity on our productive and sustainable enterprise, to develop a healthier ecosystem and fertile country by creating clear run off and sequestering carbon. Our interest lies in building and sustaining a thriving soil microbiome, built organically, to support a resilient ecosystem for a healthy world. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? What do you currently use for monitoring and record keeping? Maia Grazing app, Long Paddock forage reports, VegeMachine reports, Cibo Labs via MLA reports. Do you use any predictive modelling to assist in management decisions? Maia and RCS spreadsheets Do you currently have a detailed farm map including paddock mapping? engagements.subject: Re: Soil Carbon Proposal Plan - Update
engagements.body: Hi Dan, I hope you're well. As an FYI - we will be likely moving to a more regular position where all of our landholders and partners will be required to have their own ANREU account to hold their ACCUs (this is the same set up Adam Gunthorpe has for his ACCU's essentially) Setting up an ANREU account can be done via the CER's website; or we can do it on behalf of the landholder once your Key Commercial Terms have bene signed. https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance What this means, is we have a number of marking positives and offerings that can be put to the landholder. We can absolutely set up an ANREU account for you Landholder has full flexibility and autonomy of their ACCUs You can elect to sell either through AgriProve or on their own, or through another broker This avoids a brokerage fee or holding fee from AgriProve if they have their ACCUs transferred and broker through someone else. We will look for formalise a process for setting up these accounts, starting with our landholders who have already been issued credits, and then working through clients with a measured increase and then onto clients as a part of their onboarding/re-sampling. engagements.subject: RE: Feedback from solicitors
engagements.body: Hi Dan and Emma-Jane, Thank-you again for taking the time to meet with me on Tuesday. I greatly appreciated the visit and the opportunity to discuss in further detail the Stonehaven Soil Carbon Project. Following up on our conversations and the actions that I have committed to you from that meeting, please see below: Action Item: Clarifications to clauses 13.3 and 14.3 to align with the explanations in the letter. This is a two part approach, firstly, we are happy to include these explanations as an appendix to the Key Commercial Terms, that we can sign-off and agree on. Clarification of Project Termination (once again, happy to include this into the appendix, so that it is agreed and signed). 13. Default and Termination 13.1 Where there is an Event of Default which is not remedied within 30 Business Days the non-defaulting party may choose to terminate this Agreement by giving written notice to the defaulting party. Event of Default means: (1) a material breach of this Agreement; (2) any failure to pay any amount or transfer any ACCUs in accordance with the Agreement; or (3) an Insolvency Event. 13.3 states: “Operator may terminate this Agreement if the parties, acting in good faith, agree there is no reasonable pathway to keep the Carbon Projects operational. In such circumstances, the Operator must: …” Under the Default and Termination clause, and assuming the agreement has not been terminated in line with Clause 2.3 (i.e. the project in unviable prior to the first reporting and issuance of ACCUs), AgriProve does not have rights to terminate the agreement. Clause 13.3 requires that both parties agree to terminate the project while acting in good faith. If AgriProve were to instigate and insist on a project termination due to our assessment that it was unviable for AgriProve to continue, you as a landholder/operator have the rights within this agreement to deny that termination of the project. If AgriProve were to continue down this path without your consent, then it would be likely be determined that we would be in breach of our good faith obligations, and that would constitute a material breach of the agreement. We would then be required to pay all costs associated and outlined as per 13.2. If the project was revoked, it would be our responsibility to return all ACCUs to the project, as we would have materially breached the agreement. This is of course, under the assumption that you as a landholder have: * Complied with all obligations under the LMS and Methodology * Reasonably believe the project remains viable for your business * Declines to agree that the termination is necessary. The second part, are the following drafted clauses: Amendment to 13.3(2) - (2) pay all outstanding fees and costs owed to AgriProve including the equivalent dollar value of any Additional Product and Services Fee ACCUs previously agreed. For the avoidance of doubt, where no Project ACCUs have been issued to the Carbon Projects as at the date of termination under this clause 13.3, and any baseline soil sampling costs have been met by the Operator in accordance with clause 8.2, no further fees or costs shall be payable by the Operator or Landholder to AgriProve; Lastly, and as discussed, it is not in our interest to revoke projects, this is out of line with our business strategy. If there was no pathway for our relationship to continue, and operate the project, then it would be transferring the project proponent and removal of AgriProve from project operation as per Clause 9. Please let me know any feedback following the above, and we can progress. I think (outside of the previously updated clauses (Biosecurity)) and the amendment to 13.3(2), the simplest option rather than re-drafting clauses, is to add the explanations and statements made in these emails as an appendix, and if approved, we can incorporate as an appendix to the KCT; so it is clear and agreed. Thanks again for your time on Tuesday, Kind regards, Will Frecheville | Head of Operat…

engagements.subject: RE: Feedback from solicitors
engagements.body: Hi Dan and Emma-Jane, Thanks for your time with Will last week. I've attached yourHORIZON: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PHVIKD2MOV0 Snapshot, which shows the estimated opportunity based on our analysis. You have 1,129 eligible hectares across the property. Your Dermosols and Chromosols, which make up over 90% of the eligible area, create conditions suited to carbon building, and the Vertosol component adds further capacity through its high water holding and carbon stability attributes. With 659mm of annual rainfall, the property sits in a rainfall band that supports meaningful accumulation under improved management practices. The analysis shows Strength Zones concentrated through the northern boundary paddocks and upper-left block, where modelled carbon levels currently sit above the property median. Opportunity Zones are prominent across the lower-centre and south-central paddocks of the middle and eastern blocks — where targeted management could support carbon gains across a substantial share of the property. We're projecting approximately 84,750 ACCUs over 25 years, supported across 3 registerable projects based on our rainfall band methodology. The eligible area shown is derived from automated satellite analysis and should be treated as a reference. Our geospatial team conducts a detailed property assessment as part of the next stage, combining expert interpretation with your on-ground knowledge. Let me know if you'd like to jump on a call to talk it through.
