engagements.subject: Carbon Project Crediting Meeting
engagements.body: Online meeting to discuss the carbon project and putting the actions in place to get the information we need. ________________________________________________________________________________ Microsoft Teams Need help? Join the meeting now Meeting ID: 435 737 614 880 Passcode: eqsJHx For organizers: Meeting options | Reset dial-in PIN ________________________________________________________________________________

QTR Check - 19/11/2024 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Eligible activities: · Applying nutrients · Retaining stubble 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? No nutrients put on in the last 3 months, season not good enough to put anything onto crops. Have put 4t CalciPrill over 80ha (50kg/ha) on to pasture paddocks on project 2. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Usually apply gypsum every march where beans are planted and lime every second year, around 150ha. Have sprayed out project 2 and transitioning to crop. 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Yes, new. 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 25% on project 2 only. 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} 12-month period 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} 3 years, aiming for a 4-year rotation of crops and then grazed off. 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 40ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? AgWorld for all cropping, fert/chemical. No notes taken for the sheep. Just buy the sheep in and fatten them and sell them. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? No noticeable changes in the last 6 months, although plants did look more robust, improved vigor with the VAM seed coating. Lack of rain lately. 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? None. 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? None. 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? Happy so far, Harry at LawrieCo has been keeping him up to date.

engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Barwick CPs
engagements.body: Dear Geoff and Donna, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. QTR Check - 19/11/2024 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Eligible activities: · Applying nutrients · Retaining stubble 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? No nutrients put on in the last 3 months, season not good enough to put anything onto crops. Have put 4t CalciPrill over 80ha (50kg/ha) on to pasture paddocks on project 2. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Usually apply gypsum every march where beans are planted and lime every second year, around 150ha. Have sprayed out project 2 and transitioning to crop. 4. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Barwick CPs
engagements.body: Dear Geoff and Donna, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. If you have any questions related compliance or data protection, please contact our Data Protection Officer . engagements.subject: FW: Variation of ERF170337 Barwick Carbon Project 4 [SEC=OFFICIAL]

engagements.body: QTR Check - 19/11/2024 - OPS010 - Project Monitoring and Reporting 1. Eligible activities: · Applying nutrients · Retaining stubble 2. Has your selected management activities been actively implemented over the last 3 months? No nutrients put on in the last 3 months, season not good enough to put anything onto crops. Have put 4t CalciPrill over 80ha (50kg/ha) on to pasture paddocks on project 2. 3. What is your plan to implement these management activities for the next 3 months? Usually apply gypsum every march where beans are planted and lime every second year, around 150ha. Have sprayed out project 2 and transitioning to crop. 4. Has the implementation of these activities been new, or does it represent a change in management relative to management prior to your project being baselined? Yes, new. 5. Over what proportion of your overall project area have these activities been implemented to date? 25% on project 2 only. 6. What is the Average Grazing duration per paddock target? (time, days) {*Grazing Projects only} 12-month period 7. How long is your rest period target? {*Grazing Projects only} 3 years, aiming for a 4-year rotation of crops and then grazed off. 8. What is the Average Size in Hectares per paddock? {*Grazing Projects only} 40ha 9. How are you keeping records of these management activities (farm management software, hand-written notes, spreadsheet)? AgWorld for all cropping, fert/chemical. No notes taken for the sheep. Just buy the sheep in and fatten them and sell them. 10. Have you observed any positive or negative changes in your operation since implementing these activities (for example increased productivity, improved soil health)? No noticeable changes in the last 6 months, although plants did look more robust, improved vigor with the VAM seed coating. Lack of rain lately. 11. Have you been impacted by any unforeseen circumstances related to your carbon project over the last 3 months (such as bushfire, flood, drought)? None. 12. Have there been any changes to your carbon project area over the last quarter (such as additional infrastructure, tree plantings)? None. 13. Is there anything further AgriProve can do to assist in the operation of your soil carbon project? Happy so far, Harry at LawrieCo has been keeping him up to date.

engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 - Farm Management Records
engagements.body: Hi Leonie and David, Thank you for returning the management records document. Regarding the possibility of relinquishment of ACCUs in the event of sale and the incoming owners electing not to continue the project. AgriProve’s Master Terms and Conditions addresses this in the event of sale. Clause 2.7 states that “if Operator is to cease being the operator of any Project Property, Landholder and Operator agree to notify AgriProve as soon as they are aware and to novate this agreement…” This means that the incoming buyers would need to (for the purposes of the project) become the Operator and the project continues. If, however, they would like to cease “implementation” of the project, then they would notify AgriProve of their intent to cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities as per clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions. They would then allow AgriProve to come to the property and complete the required soil testing to ensure we meet our reporting obligations to keep the project registered and compliant with the ERF. This would mean, in all operational aspects, that as long as the land remained in an agricultural system, and this process is followed, that the project is no longer ‘active’ (in the form of implementation), however it is still compliant to the ERF. This indemnifies both the outgoing landholder and incoming landholder of any requirement to relinquish ACCUs. Furthermore, there is no cost obligation to the incoming landholder, as AgriProve bears the costs of any subsequent sampling, auditing requirements, and reporting/administrative requirements for the project. Hope that answers the query appropriately, please let me know if you require more information. engagements.body: Good morning Leonie and David, Congratulations on your recent ACCU issuance for Ryan Carbon Project 2 and thank you for your patience. We require this information to pay the $30 (excl. GST) licence fee to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon project for the term of the agreement. Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Ryan CPs
engagements.body: Dear Leonie and David, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 - Farm Management Records
engagements.body: Hi Leonie and David, Thank you for returning the management records document. Regarding the possibility of relinquishment of ACCUs in the event of sale and the incoming owners electing not to continue the project. AgriProve’s Master Terms and Conditions addresses this in the event of sale. Clause 2.7 states that “if Operator is to cease being the operator of any Project Property, Landholder and Operator agree to notify AgriProve as soon as they are aware and to novate this agreement…” This means that the incoming buyers would need to (for the purposes of the project) become the Operator and the project continues. If, however, they would like to cease “implementation” of the project, then they would notify AgriProve of their intent to cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities as per clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions. They would then allow AgriProve to come to the property and complete the required soil testing to ensure we meet our reporting obligations to keep the project registered and compliant with the ERF. This would mean, in all operational aspects, that as long as the land remained in an agricultural system, and this process is followed, that the project is no longer ‘active’ (in the form of implementation), however it is still compliant to the ERF. This indemnifies both the outgoing landholder and incoming landholder of any requirement to relinquish ACCUs. Furthermore, there is no cost obligation to the incoming landholder, as AgriProve bears the costs of any subsequent sampling, auditing requirements, and reporting/administrative requirements for the project. Hope that answers the query appropriately, please let me know if you require more information. engagements.subject: RE: Ryan Carbon Project 2 ACCU Issuance
engagements.body: Hi Leonie, I think that you are referring to the cash prepayment option for ACCU distribution, where AgriProve makes a cash prepayment for ACCUs to the project operator in advance of the ACCUs being generated at a fixed price of $12.50 per ACCU. This option would be selected at the start of the carbon project in the Sale and Licence Agreement and is based on the prepayment to AgriProve at an agreed price of $12.50 for ACCUs from a buyer. Based on your selection of option 3 in the Sale and Licence Agreement to 'hold ACCUs for future sale', your ACCUs will be held in AgriProve's Registry of Emissions Units Account (ANREAU) on trust for sale at a later date nominated by you for the best price available. AgriProve will act as a market broker for the ACCUs, and a brokerage fee of $0.375 per ACCU will be charged. These ACCUs could also be transferred to the Operators stand-alone ANREU account if established. engagements.subject: Leonie Doran and Hobbs Catch up
Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Ryan CPs
engagements.body: Dear Leonie and David, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. The idea is to show what’s actually happening on the ground and how soil carbon projects turn into real outcomes for producers and the broader market. If you’re coming along, it’d be great to see you there or have a chat at the stand afterwards. All the best, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io On Sunday, 19 October 2025, 9:37:09 am +1100, Claudia Bryant wrote: Hi Peter , I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is coming up soon - it’s on 3–6 November in Albury. AgriProve will be there again this year. Our Chair, Matthew Warnken, is helping MC parts of the event, and we’re also co-sponsoring the Soil Carbon Day on the Tuesday. A few of us from the team will be around across the three days, so if you’re attending, it’d be great to catch up for a chat about your project or anything happening on farm. Here’s the link if you’d like to check out the program: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/: https://nationalcarbonfarmingconference.com/ Hope to see you there, Claudia Bryant Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist Phone: +61483969401 Mobile: +61498664218 Email: claudia@agriprove.io: mailto:claudia@agriprove.io

engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lyne CP
engagements.body: Dear Peter, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Lynch Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Hi Derek, Thank you for your patience with us completing your annual review. The review is based on Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE), a dataset obtained from satellite imagery that is used measure, model, and track seasonal changes in chlorophyll concentration. Improvements in NDRE relative to the baseline period are used to indicate the potential for increases in soil organic carbon to have occurred on the project. The increase from the previous period to the current period has not met our threshold (shown in the attached report), we will not be resampling this year. Your project will be reviewed again next year. Note that we have a requirement under the method to sample your project a minimum of once every five years. I am working on the other items that we discussed on Friday regarding T0-T1 results and an overlay of your paddocks with the carbon project boundaries. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Annual Review
engagements.body: Good Morning Derek, I have just completed the Annual Satellite review of your carbon project. We do these every 12 months using satellite imagery of the NDRE ( Normalized Difference Red Edge) on your farm to get an idea of if the vegetation has indicated that carbon sequestration is likely to have occurred in the past 12 months and we should resample at this time. As you will see in the attached document, your projects average NDRE has had a negative trend when compared to the baseline period. This does not mean that carbon has gone backwards; it means that compared to baseline the average trend has not be positive comparatively - which is an indicator that carbon sequestration has been unlikely at this time. This result means that your project has not met our threshold for us to complete resampling this year. We will review this again next year or when our HORIZON model is fully up and running to decide if resampling would be worthwhile then. if you have any questions or would like to touch base about your carbon project- feel free to call me anytime. From: Stephen Warnken Sent: Tuesday, 3 March 2026 12:14 PM To: 'Koolah Trust' Subject: RE: ACCU Distribution - Lynch Carbon Project Hi Derek, Thank you for your letter of 27 February 2026. We have reviewed your position carefully and write to respond formally in relation to the Additional Project Work and Services Fee for baseline soil sampling services under the Agreement. The Agreed Fee We respectfully disagree with the position set out in your letter. The terms of Schedule 3 of the Agreement are clear and unambiguous. The agreed Additional Project Work and Services Fee for Baseline Soil Sampling Services is stated as: “750 ACCUs @ $6.66” The fee is denominated in ACCUs. The figure of $6.66 per ACCU recorded in Schedule 3 reflects the prevailing risk-adjusted ACCU reference price at the time the Agreement was executed in November 2020. It was included to provide context as to the dollar-equivalent value of the fee at that time – consistent with how the Agreement records carbon pricing more broadly (as identified in Schedule 1). It does not, and was never intended to, convert the fee into a fixed dollar obligation or to cap AgriProve’s entitlement at a dollar value. There is no mechanism in the Agreement to convert an ACCU entitlement into a variable dollar amount based on prevailing spot prices at the time of issuance. Commitments Made in Reliance on the Agreement In discharging its responsibilities under the Agreement, and in good faith reliance on the terms of Schedule 3, AgriProve entered into downstream obligations and commitments that have already required the delivery of ACCUs from this project. Those commitments were made on the reasonable assumption that AgriProve would receive the ACCUs to which it is contractually entitled. To the extent those obligations have now been enforced, AgriProve has complied with them in full. AgriProve’s Position That said, we believe the most practical and sensible time to resolve the allocation of ACCUs under Schedule 3 is at the point of the next project issuance, when ACCUs are available for distribution. We propose that both parties defer this discussion until that time, at which point we can meet to agree the final allocation in light of ACCUs issued and the terms of the Agreement. Next Steps AgriProve will be in touch ahead of the next issuance to arrange a suitable time to discuss. In the meantime, if you have any questions or wish to raise anything further, please do not hesitate to contact me. engagements.subject: Action Required: Carbon Project Licence and ANREU Account Set-Up - Lynch CP
engagements.body: Dear Derek, We have recently completed a review and have identified some items that need actioning. We require the following to be completed: 1. Complete and return the Bank Details Request Form This to pay you the Carbon Project Licence as per our contract 1. Set up an ANREU Account via the CER's Online Services Portal. This to transfer your ACCUs that you have earned to you, to give you the flexibility to commercialise how you chose. Complete the Bank Details Request Form (attached) Under AgriProve's Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve is granted a licence to operate, monitor, measure, and audit your carbon projects for term of the agreement. AgriProve pays a $1.00 per year fee (excl. GST) for this licence, with the full $30.00 (excl. GST) to be paid in full upon lodging a project report with the Clean Energy Regulator ($1 for each of the projects 25 years, plus $1 per year - allowing up to 5 years prior to lodgement of the first project report). We will also require this information if we sell any ACCUs on your behalf to enable us to pay you for the purchase of your ACCUs as set out under the ACCU sale options in our Key Commercial Terms. If you do not wish to send these details over via email, please feel free to call myself, @Dylan Jones or @Claudia Bryant to provide. Prior to payment, we may also call to confirm that details are correct. Opening an ANREU (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units) Account. For AgriProve to transfer your entitlement of ACCUs issued to your carbon project, you need to have your own ANREU account. This process is similar to applying for a passport, where you need to verify your identity, and complete some forms to allow for the CER to set up the account. Broadly there are 5-steps to this process: 1. Set up and create an Online Services Account (https://onlineservices.cer.gov.au/). This is no different to setting up a standard online account. 2. Type "ANREU" in the search bar, and select the tile that states 'Open an ANREU account' - walk through the pages and complete the online forms. 3. You will need to select "Register an Individual" or "Register an Organisation" as a part of this process. Both options 4. Complete a Police Check (download the appropriately filled out form and get signed OR there is an option where the CER completes this task for you). 5. Submit the Application and once approved provide the ANREU account number to AgriProve. We will then transfer your ACCUs to you within 10-business days of receiving the Account #. We have some resources available to assist in this process. If you have any difficulty, please feel free to reach out. * Attached '240611 AgriProve ANREU Application - Template' document which steps through the process and the application information requirements * CER Account creation guidance found here: https://cer.gov.au/online-systems/anreu-account-guidance * Further guidance we have created on our website following initial feedback: https://help.agriprove.io/setting-up-your-anreu-account The process is a little clunky, but should be reasonably straightforward. I know the CER has made a big effort to make this process simpler.
